papers.title: Tumo​r-associated macrophages in ovarian, prostate, thyroid and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors: molecular crosstalk and therapeutic perspectives.
papers.abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are key regulators of the tumor microenvironment and play dual roles in endocrine cancer progression by exhibiting remarkable functional plasticity beyond the conventional M1/M2 paradigm. Their interactions with tumor cells influence immune evasion, angiogenesis, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance through complex signaling networks and extracellular vesicle-mediated communication. This review summarizes the current understanding of TAM biology across some key endocrine and hormone-dependent cancers, including ovarian, prostate, thyroid, and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, highlighting their prognostic significance and molecular mechanisms. We further discuss emerging TAM-targeted therapeutic strategies, including macrophage depletion, immune checkpoint modulation, macrophage reprogramming, and nanoparticle-based approaches. Finally, we outline the challenges associated with clinical translation and emphasize the potential of single-cell and multi-omics technologies to enable precision macrophage-targeted therapies for endocrine cancers, including a summary of recent developments in the field of precision mapping of TAMs.

papers.title: Childhood insulinoma after years of recurrent hypoglycemia: the role of GLP-1 receptor imaging.
papers.abstract: To highlight the diagnostic challenges of childhood insulinoma and the complementary role of GLP-1 receptor-targeted imaging in localizing a small pancreatic lesion. A 12-year-old boy had a history of recurrent episodes suggestive of hypoglycemia reportedly beginning at approximately 4 years of age, with reported glucose concentrations as low as 15-20 mg/dL and associated night sweats. Diagnostic evaluation was fragmented over several years due to frequent family relocations. During a critical sample, plasma glucose was 37 mg/dL, with insulin 105.2 µIU/mL and C-peptide 5.48 ng/mL, supporting endogenous hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia. MRI demonstrated a small lesion in the pancreatic body. 68Ga-Exendin-4 PET/CT demonstrated focal GLP-1 receptor-targeted uptake corresponding to the pancreatic lesion, with a delayed SUVmax of 9.1. The patient underwent open surgical enucleation. Histopathology demonstrated a 1.7-cm well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor, WHO Grade 1, with a Ki-67 index of 1 %, negative margins, and no necrosis, lymphovascular, or perineural invasion. Postoperatively, glucose concentrations remained normal. Persistent or unexplained hypoglycemia in children warrants consideration of insulinoma when endogenous hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia is demonstrated. In this case, GLP-1 receptor-targeted imaging provided complementary functional localization alongside MRI and supported focused curative surgery.
papers.journal: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

papers.title: Melanoma Metastasis to a Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumor: A Case Report and Literature Review.
papers.abstract: We report a 44-year-old man with a non-functioning pituitary macroadenoma diagnosed approximately 10 years before the current presentation. He subsequently developed metastatic amelanotic melanoma originating from a cutaneous lesion of the right auricle, with jejunal metastases. After disease progression despite immunotherapy and chemotherapy, he presented with visual disturbances and panhypopituitarism. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a 28 × 22 × 30 mm endo-suprasellar mass compressing the optic chiasm. The patient underwent endoscopic transnasal transsphenoidal resection. Histopathological and immunohistochemical examination identified two tumors of distinct histogenesis within the same specimen: a pituitary adenoma and metastatic melanoma. The melanoma component was positive for Melan-A, HMB-45, SOX10, and S-100, confirming melanoma metastasis to the pituitary adenoma and establishing tumor-to-tumor metastasis. Postoperatively, the patient's visual function improved, and he was discharged on postoperative Day 5. This case demonstrates the diagnostic value of thorough histopathological and immunohistochemical evaluation when the clinical behavior of a previously diagnosed sellar lesion changes in a patient with systemic malignancy. Surgical decompression improved visual function and provided a definitive tissue diagnosis, supporting coordinated multidisciplinary management.

papers.title: Pathological nodal involvement and recurrence risk after resection of typical pulmonary carcinoids: A single-centre cohort study.
papers.abstract: Although typical pulmonary carcinoids (TC) are generally associated with excellent long-term outcomes, a subset of patients develops recurrence after complete resection. Current risk stratification largely relies on tumour size and TNM stage, yet the prognostic determinants of recurrence remain poorly defined. We aimed to identify clinicopathological predictors of recurrence in a homogeneous cohort of resected typical pulmonary carcinoids. We retrospectively analysed consecutive patients undergoing surgical resection for pathologically confirmed TC between 2016 and 2022 at a high-volume thoracic surgery centre. Recurrence-free survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, with deaths occurring without documented recurrence censored at the time of death. Univariable Cox regression identified factors associated with recurrence, and parsimonious multivariable models were constructed according to the number of events. Among 115 patients, 97 had complete follow-up; six recurred (6.2%) after a median follow-up of 60.9 months. Nodal positivity showed the strongest recurrence signal and remained associated with recurrence in a parsimonious model including tumour size HR 7.40 (95% CI 1.49-36.83; p = 0.014). Positive node count and lymph node ratio were associated with recurrence in exploratory analyses (both p < 0.001) but were not assessed for incremental value beyond pN. Tumour size, Ki-67, surgical approach, and extent of pulmonary resection did not reach statistical significance. Node-positive patients had worse recurrence-free survival (p = 0.002). In this single-centre cohort of resected typical pulmonary carcinoids, pathological nodal involvement showed a stronger association with recurrence than tumour size. Given the limited number of recurrence events, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger multicentre cohorts before informing postoperative risk stratification or surveillance strategies.

papers.title: A hypodiploid corticotroph pituitary tumor with a germline TP53 variant.
papers.abstract: Li-Fraumeni syndrome (LFS), caused by germline TP53 mutations, predisposes to a wide spectrum of malignancies, but an association with pituitary tumors has not been definitively established. We performed germline sequencing on 20 patients with aggressive pituitary tumors. Pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants were identified in three patients: one high-penetrant variant, TP53 (NM_000546) c.799C>T (p.Arg267Trp), and two low-penetrant variants that are likely incidental findings: LZTR1 (NM_006767) c.1214delG (p.Gly405Alafs*56) and MUTYH (NM_001128425) c.536A>G (p.Tyr179Cys). The patient diagnosed with LFS presented in her 20s with an aggressive, silent corticotroph pituitary tumor that progressed within 5 months of the initial subtotal transsphenoidal resection. Molecular analysis identified biallelic inactivation of TP53 and widespread chromosomal loss-of-heterozygosity (cLOH) involving 8 of the 12 chromosomes frequently lost in aggressive corticotroph tumors with somatic TP53 mutations. Biallelic TP53 inactivation and the presence of cLOH supports that the germline TP53 mutation functions as a driver.

papers.title: Merkel cell carcinoma: Lessons from a review of 15 year outcomes of the multidisciplinary management at a UK tertiary referral centre.
papers.abstract: Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) is a rare, aggressive skin cancer with high mortality, low survival and propensity for recurrence and metastasis. Worldwide data on MCC patient outcomes are limited. What can we learn from our experience of a UK tertiary referral centre, over a 15 year period? Guy's Cancer Centre registry was retrospectively reviewed for MCC patients diagnosed between 2008 and 2022. Electronic medical records were reviewed for demographics, tumour characteristics, treatment modalities and outcomes including all-cause mortality. We aimed to identify the incidence and outcomes from the multidisciplinary management of this rare disease. 81 cases of MCC were included (55% male, mean age at presentation 71.4 years, range 40-93 years, SD 11.2). Mean follow-up was 4.1 years. 40% presented with metastatic disease, 42% of these had regional lymph node metastases. 15 patients underwent sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB), 40% of these were positive. SLNB provided accurate staging and guided adjuvant treatment but did not appear to confer a survival benefit. Adjuvant treatments of radiotherapy and systemic therapy have evolved to be added in over the years. This single-centre study examines long-term MCC outcomes in a UK population that is comparable to published data. Our data suggests SLNB positivity may confer prognostic value. We suggest rapid and earlier treatment is best. Hence working these patients up in a specialist skin (Melanoma) MDM makes sense given the options of adjuvant radiotherapy and systemic therapies, where adverse events can be managed. Given the paucity of data worldwide, we hope our experience will support clinicians in counselling patients on treatment options. Survival data alone may not represent the optimum measure of a good outcome. Non-clinical factors, such as social support and transport issues may influence the outcomes more than final treatment given. Patients' and their care-givers' partnerships should be encouraged in the decision-making process. Treatment accepted may not reflect pathways of guidance proffered due to the changing landscape of options and individual patient choice.

papers.title: Schwannoma of the Transverse Mesocolon: A Neurogenic Rarity.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Colonic schwannomas are rare benign neurogenic tumors originating from Schwann cells of the peripheral nerve sheath, and account for a very small proportion of gastrointestinal mesenchymal neoplasms. Their nonspecific clinical and radiological appearance often leads to diagnostic dilemma. Definitive diagnosis relies on histopathological and immunohistochemical evaluation. Preoperative diagnosis remains particularly challenging because colonic schwannomas may mimic other mesenchymal or cystic lesions, including gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GISTs) and duplication cysts. CASE REPORT We present the case of a 67-year-old asymptomatic male patient with a schwannoma of the transverse colon wall diagnosed only after surgical excision, through histopathological and immunohistochemical examination. After upper and lower endoscopy revealed no mucosal abnormalities, computed tomography suggested a duplication cyst, while magnetic resonance imaging favored a GIST arising from the transverse colon. Due to the uncertain preoperative diagnosis and the size and location of the lesion, transverse colectomy with primary anastomosis was performed. Histopathological examination demonstrated a spindle-cell tumor with very low mitotic activity and no necrosis. Immunohistochemistry showed positivity for S-100 and SOX10 and negativity for CD117, CD34, and DOG1, confirming the diagnosis of schwannoma. Complete R0 excision was achieved, and the patient remained recurrence-free 2 years later. CONCLUSIONS This case emphasizes the diagnostic challenge and the importance of considering schwannoma in differential diagnosis of colonic intramural masses extending into the transverse mesocolon. The predominantly intramural and exophytic growth pattern may account for both the normal endoscopic findings and the misleading radiological appearance. Complete surgical excision with negative margins is associated with an excellent prognosis for benign colorectal schwannomas.
papers.journal: The American journal of case reports

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Skin Cancer Detection: Is Clinical Deployment Outpacing Experimental Validation?
papers.abstract: Deep neural networks classify dermoscopic and clinical images of skin lesions with accuracy that matches, and in curated comparisons exceeds, experienced dermatologists. Regulators have responded: an elastic scattering spectroscopy device with an embedded classifier is authorised for primary care in the United States, an image-based system has conditional approval in the National Health Service, and consumer applications are marketed directly to the public. In this Viewpoint we argue that clinical deployment is advancing faster than the experimental evidence that investigative dermatology would normally demand. Performance measured on internal test sets falls when algorithms are exposed to external images, non-dermoscopic photographs or other populations. Networks learn confounders, such as surgical ink markings, as readily as morphology, and the histopathological reference standard is itself subject to substantial observer variation. Public training datasets record skin phototype for about 2% of images and contain almost no darkest-phototype, acral or nail images. Regulated devices with prospective evidence achieve high sensitivity or negative predictive value at the cost of low specificity, shifting referral and biopsy rates with unmeasured effects on patient outcomes and overdiagnosis, and the single randomised trial to date improved diagnostic accuracy, chiefly among non-dermatologists, without measuring those outcomes. We identify where the largest gains lie, in primary care, allied health and under-served regions, and propose an experimental agenda: phototype-stratified external validation, shortcut-detection and counterfactual explanation studies, consensus histopathological labelling, pragmatic randomised trials with outcome endpoints reported to CONSORT-AI, and post-market surveillance under the European Medical Device Regulation and Artificial Intelligence Act.

papers.title: When Thyrotropin Meets Growth Hormone: The Clinical Challenges of a Mixed GH/TSH-Secreting PIT1-Lineage Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumour.
papers.abstract: Background: Acromegaly is most commonly caused by a growth hormone (GH)-secreting pituitary neuroendocrine tumour (PitNET). Plurihormonal PIT1-lineage PitNETs are uncommon, and combined GH and thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) secretion poses distinctive diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. We report a mixed GH/TSH-secreting PIT1-lineage PitNET in which the biochemical response to preoperative lanreotide supported the clinical suspicion of a functionally relevant thyrotroph component before targeted pathological reassessment. Case Presentation: A 39-year-old woman presented with a two-year history of progressive acral enlargement, headaches, hyperhidrosis, snoring, and voice deepening. Biochemical evaluation showed IGF-1 1128 ng/mL (reference range 93.1-281), GH 61 µg/L, TSH 1.5 µIU/mL (0.35-4.94), FT4 1.66 ng/dL (0.7-1.5), and FT3 7.0 pg/mL (1.8-4.2). Pituitary MRI demonstrated a 15 × 14 × 10.5 mm macroadenoma. Lanreotide 120 mg every four weeks reduced IGF-1 to 846 ng/mL and GH to 14 µg/L while normalizing FT4 (1.04 ng/dL) and FT3 (3.9 pg/mL), reinforcing the suspicion of mixed GH/TSH secretion. Transsphenoidal surgery was performed in October 2024. The tumour was initially classified as a densely granulated somatotroph PitNET; prompted by the preoperative biochemical phenotype, additional β-TSH immunostaining demonstrated positivity in numerous tumour cells, leading to reclassification as a mature plurihormonal PIT1-lineage PitNET (Ki-67 approximately 1%). Postoperative biochemical remission was not achieved, and MRI demonstrated a 7 mm residual lesion. Lanreotide was resumed, with the sustained control of the thyrotroph component but persistent GH/IGF-1 excess. Because residual disease persisted with slight cavernous sinus extension, Gamma Knife radiosurgery was performed in July 2026. Conclusions: Mixed GH/TSH-secreting PIT1-lineage PitNETs may be overlooked when TSH is inappropriately normal rather than frankly elevated. This case illustrates the value of integrating biochemical findings, treatment response, and targeted histopathological reassessment. Persistent disease despite surgery and somatostatin receptor ligand therapy further highlights the frequent need for multimodal, long-term management.

papers.title: 68Ga-DOTATOC PET/CT Uptake and Physiological Impairment in DIPNECH: An Exploratory Case Series.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Diffuse idiopathic pulmonary neuroendocrine cell hyperplasia (DIPNECH) can cause respiratory symptoms and physiological impairment. We explored whether quantitative somatostatin-receptor imaging by positron emission tomography/computed tomography with gallium-68-labelled DOTATOC (68Ga-DOTATOC PET/CT) is associated with pulmonary physiology and nodule count in histologically confirmed DIPNECH. Methods: This retrospective, single-centre, hypothesis-generating series included six consecutive adults diagnosed during 2020-2025. Spearman correlations with exact permutation p-values and 95% confidence intervals related the maximum standardised uptake value (SUVmax) of the most avid lesion to diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO), forced expiratory flow between 25% and 75% of forced vital capacity (FEF25-75) and the ratio of forced expiratory volume in 1 s to forced vital capacity (FEV1/FVC); index-lesion diameter and expected partial-volume recovery were examined. Analyses were exploratory and unadjusted for multiple comparisons. Results: All patients were women. SUVmax correlated inversely with DLCO (ρ = -0.90; p = 0.028) and FEF25-75 (ρ = -0.84; p = 0.044); the nodule-count-DLCO association was uncertain (ρ = -0.37; p = 0.50). Index lesions measured 3.6-4.7 mm, below the resolution of the PET system; lesion diameter was unrelated to SUVmax (ρ = -0.20), and the association with DLCO persisted after crude recovery correction (ρ = -0.66). Conclusions: Higher 68Ga-DOTATOC uptake of the most avid lesion accompanied greater physiological impairment in this six-patient series, and the differences in uptake were not explained by lesion size. Given the sample size, wide confidence intervals, multiple unadjusted comparisons, unadjusted comorbidities and sub-resolution lesions, these findings are hypothesis-generating only; they do not establish SUVmax as a marker of disease severity, an actionable threshold or a guide to biopsy, but support prospective investigation of somatostatin-receptor imaging in DIPNECH.

papers.title: Procalcitonin in Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma: An Umbrella Review of Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Procalcitonin has been proposed as an alternative or complementary biomarker to calcitonin in medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC). We synthesised the published systematic reviews, appraised their quality, and measured their reliance on the same primary studies. Methods: Umbrella review of systematic reviews reporting measured procalcitonin values in proven or suspected MTC. PubMed/MEDLINE and the Cochrane Library were searched to 30 June 2026. Quality was appraised with AMSTAR-2 and overlap as the corrected covered area (CCA). Results: Seven evidence syntheses (2015-2024) were included, four addressing procalcitonin itself and two with meta-analysis. Across diagnostic and monitoring populations, a bivariate meta-analysis of 11 studies and 5817 patients gave sensitivity of 0.90 (95% CI 0.71-0.97) and specificity of 1.00 (95% CI 0.85-1.00); in postoperative surveillance, five studies and 296 patients gave pooled sensitivity and specificity of 96%. The five syntheses enumerating their sources drew on 21 distinct primary reports, giving a corrected covered area of 38.1%, every pairwise value above the 15% threshold for very high overlap. Two primary studies were extracted discordantly; for one of them the same data yielded specificities of 84% and 5% depending on the threshold and assay platform applied. Confidence was low for one review and critically low for six. Conclusions: Procalcitonin is a promising adjunct to calcitonin, with better analytical behaviour, but routine combined measurement is not yet supported. The apparent consistency across syntheses reflects a shared and narrow primary literature rather than independent replication, and the absence of an agreed, method-specific threshold remains the main barrier to implementation.

papers.title: Targeted Screening Studies on Endemic Propolis Extracts for Selective Cytotoxicity Against Human Melanoma Cells Models.
papers.abstract: Melanoma is the most aggressive and life-threatening form of skin cancer. Propolis possesses diverse biological activities and is considered a promising source of compounds for anticancer therapy. This study evaluated the cytotoxic effects of propolis from endemic regions of Nepal, Greece, Kazakhstan, Ukraine, and Georgia on melanoma cell lines (A375, SK-MEL-3) and normal human skin fibroblasts (BJ). Chemical characterization was performed using UHPLC-UV-ESI-qTOF-MS/MS. Total flavonoid and polyphenol contents, as well as antioxidant activity, were also determined. Biological effects were assessed by measuring cell viability, apoptosis (fluorescent staining and confocal microscopy), and caspase-6 activity (fluorometric assay). Most analyzed extracts contained markers characteristic of black poplar-type propolis, including chrysin, pinocembrin, galangin, pinobanksin-3-acetate, and caffeic acid monoesters such as caffeic acid phenethyl ester (CAPE) and isomers of the 1,1-dimethylallyl ester. Three propolis samples from Georgia showed the strongest anticancer activity against melanoma cells while exhibiting low toxicity toward normal fibroblasts (SI > 1). These extracts also displayed high antioxidant activity and elevated polyphenol content. Apoptosis predominated in A375 cells, whereas necrosis was more evident in SK-MEL-3 cells, consistent with increased caspase-6 activity in A375 cells. These results suggest that Georgian propolis may be a promising candidate for further investigation in melanoma therapy.

papers.title: Indocyanine Green and Technetium-99m: CT-Guided Marking of Lung Nodules Before Robotic-Assisted Lung Resection.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: For stage I non-small cell lung cancer, surgery remains the cornerstone of treatment and the use of minimally invasive techniques is desirable. The lack of tactile feedback in RATS is a well-known drawback of this approach, so precise identification of the disease is crucial for performing lung resection. Methods: We present our retrospective case history, accounting for 83 patients, which were divided into two groups based on marking technique: 99mTc-MAA (99mTechnetium Albumin Macroaggregates) only (Tech group) (22 cases, 26.5%) and 99mTc-MAA + Indocyanine Green (Tech + ICG group) (61 cases, 73.49%). Results: In the Tech group, there were 11 males (50%) ad 11 females (50%), the median nodule diameter was 21.5 mm (IQR 16), and the median distance of the nodule from the visceral pleura was 18 mm (IQR 21). Eighteen out of 22 nodules (81.82%) were subsolid. Three conversions were reported, all due to failure to identify the nodule (13.63%). The mean operative time was 111.6 ± 45.6 min. The histopathological examination resulted in 13 lung adenocarcinomas, one squamous cell carcinoma, two minimally invasive lung adenocarcinomas, two lung adenocarcinomas in situ, three metastases from another tumor, and one benign nodule. In the Tech + ICG group, there were 27 males (44.26%) and 34 females (55.73%), the median nodule diameter was 18 mm (IQR 14), and the median distance of the nodule from the visceral pleura was 24 mm (IQR 15). Forty-six out of 61 nodules were subsolid (75.4%). Four conversions were reported, due to failure in nodule identification (6.55%). The operative time was 105.6 ± 36.8 min. The histopathological examination resulted in 12 lung adenocarcinomas, seven squamous cell carcinomas, nine minimally invasive lung adenocarcinomas, 12 lung adenocarcinomas in situ, one typical carcinoid, seven atypical adenomatous hyperplasias, seven metastases from another tumor, and six benign nodules. The two groups are homogeneous in terms of median nodule diameter (p = 0.676), the median distance from visceral pleura (p = 0.114), SUV max (p = 0.894), operative time (p = 0.512), and nodule characteristics (solid vs. subsolid) (p = 0.724). The conversion rate was lower in the Tech + ICG group (6.55% vs. 13.63%), but the difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.375). Conclusions: Both techniques appear to be safe and reproducible. Further standardized studies are needed to validate and confirm the results obtained from our case series.

papers.title: Germline AIP Testing in Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumors: Diagnostic Yield, Variant Interpretation, and a Phenotype-Driven Clinical Approach-A Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: Germline pathogenic variants in the aryl hydrocarbon receptor-interacting protein (AIP) gene are the most common identifiable genetic cause of familial isolated pituitary adenomas (FIPA) and are particularly associated with young-onset growth hormone-secreting pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs). This review critically evaluates current evidence on patient selection for germline AIP testing, variant interpretation, and emerging multigene approaches. A narrative PubMed/MEDLINE search identified English-language studies published between January 2006 and April 2025, including original clinical studies, international cohorts, systematic reviews, consensus statements, and relevant guidelines. Evidence was synthesized with emphasis on diagnostic yield, genotype-phenotype correlations, clinical indications for testing, and contemporary American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics/Association for Molecular Pathology (ACMG/AMP) variant classification. The highest diagnostic yield is consistently observed in FIPA, pituitary gigantism, childhood- or young-onset growth hormone (GH)-secreting macroadenomas, and selected patients with aggressive or otherwise high-risk phenotypes. Contemporary ACMG/AMP classification has lowered and refined estimates of clinically actionable AIP variants compared with historical studies. Targeted AIP testing remains appropriate for characteristic phenotypes, whereas multigene panels may be useful when syndromic features, atypical presentations, or persistent suspicion of hereditary disease remain after negative AIP testing. Current evidence supports phenotype-driven rather than universal germline AIP testing in PitNETs. Integrating age at onset, family history, tumor subtype, tumor characteristics, and standardized variant interpretation may maximize diagnostic yield while limiting unnecessary testing.

papers.title: Clinical Presentation and Targeted Genetic Evaluation of Familial Isolated Pituitary Adenomas: A Single-Center Case Series.
papers.abstract: Background: Familial isolated pituitary adenomas (FIPA) are characterized by considerable clinical and genetic heterogeneity. Although germline pathogenic variants in AIP account for a subset of cases, most FIPA families remain genetically unexplained. We aimed to describe the clinical characteristics, tumor phenotype, treatment outcomes, and targeted genetic evaluation of FIPA families from a tertiary endocrine referral center. Methods: We retrospectively identified FIPA families among patients with pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs) evaluated at a tertiary endocrine referral center between 2019 and 2024. FIPA was defined as PitNETs occurring in at least two related individuals without clinical features suggestive of syndromic endocrine disease. Clinical, radiological, histopathological, and genetic data were analyzed. Results: Among 1068 patients with PitNETs, seven FIPA families were retrospectively identified (0.66% of the source cohort), comprising 20 affected individuals. Index cases included four women and three men, with a mean age at diagnosis of 37.1 ± 17.3 years. Somatotroph PitNETs predominated among index cases (5/7), whereas nonfunctioning PitNETs were more frequent among affected relatives (9/13). Six of seven index tumors were macroadenomas, and cavernous sinus invasion was present in two. No pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in AIP or MEN1 were identified by Sanger sequencing, and multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification (MLPA) detected no copy number alterations involving AIP, MEN1, or CDKN1B. Conclusions: This series highlights the clinical heterogeneity of FIPA and the differing tumor spectrum between index cases and affected relatives. The absence of pathogenic variants identified by targeted genetic testing further illustrates the genetic heterogeneity of familial pituitary tumor predisposition.

papers.title: Tryptophan and Its Selected Metabolites Modulate Melanoma-Cell Biology: A Preliminary In Vitro Study.
papers.abstract: Tryptophan (TRP) and its metabolites are involved in numerous physiological and pathological processes within the skin. They may influence melanoma biology, but their role remains insufficiently understood. This study investigated the effects of TRP, anthranilic acid (AA), and cinnabarinic acid (CBA) in melanoma cells in vitro and their potential interaction with the B-Raf proto-oncogene, serine/threonine kinase (BRAF) inhibitor vemurafenib. A375, G361, and SK-MEL-3 melanoma cell lines and a THP-1-derived macrophage model were used. Cell proliferation and metabolic activity were assessed using the 3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-2,5-diphenyltetrazolium bromide (MTT) assay, migration using a scratch assay, and cell-cycle distribution by flow cytometry. Western blotting was used to analyze selected signaling proteins. Reactive oxygen species (ROS) and nitric oxide (NO) production were evaluated. Bioinformatic analyses investigated associations between BRAF and genes related to tryptophan metabolism and the kynurenine pathway. All compounds showed dose-dependent antiproliferative effects, with prolonged exposure increasing efficacy. TRP and AA increased G0/G1 cell-cycle arrest, whereas CBA increased the G2/M population. TRP also reduced A375 cell migration. All three compounds enhanced the antiproliferative effect of vemurafenib, with CBA showing the strongest effect (approximately 20%). Western blot analysis indicated modulation of p21 expression and ERK1/2 phosphorylation, suggesting implications for cell cycle and stress signaling pathways. Moreover, conditioned medium from A375 cells exposed to tested compounds affected cell viability, ROS, and NO production in THP-1-derived macrophages. TRP and its metabolites may be considered potential supportive agents for melanoma BRAF-targeted therapy. However, further in vivo studies are needed to clarify their therapeutic value and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms.

papers.title: A Complex Molecular Profile in Melanoma: Intratumoral Heterogeneity and Therapeutic Implications.
papers.abstract: Complex molecular alterations in cancers influence tumor biology, therapeutic response, and resistance. We report a case of cutaneous melanoma demonstrating extensive intratumoral heterogeneity with important clinical implications. A 77-year-old man with stage IIA cutaneous melanoma developed an isolated nodal recurrence one year after resection. Comprehensive next-generation sequencing of the metastatic lesion revealed an uncommon genomic profile consisting of a class 3 BRAF Y472V mutation, two NF1 loss-of-function mutations, and two concurrent KIT mutations: a dominant, potentially targetable K642E mutation and a low-frequency D816V mutation associated with resistance to tyrosine kinase inhibitors. The tumor exhibited a high tumor mutational burden and microsatellite stability. The patient received neoadjuvant nivolumab plus relatlimab followed by surgical resection, achieving complete pathologic response. Repeat sequencing of the resected specimen demonstrated complete molecular clearance of all previously detected variants. This case illustrates the value of comprehensive genomic profiling in revealing biologically complex melanoma with coexisting driver and resistance-associated alterations. The presence of a treatment-naïve KIT resistance mutation suggests preexisting subclonal heterogeneity that may influence future targeted therapy, while high tumor mutational burden and NF1 loss may have contributed to the excellent response to immune checkpoint blockade.

papers.title: Regimen-Dependent Anti-Cytokine and Immune-Checkpoint Autoantibodies Are Associated with Immunotherapy Toxicity and Response in Melanoma.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) efficacy and immune-related adverse events (irAEs) in melanoma are influenced by the pre-treatment immune state. We investigated whether baseline autoantibodies directed against cytokines, chemokines, cytokine receptors, and immune-checkpoint/costimulatory proteins were associated with outcome in a regimen-dependent manner. Baseline sera from patients with metastatic melanoma were profiled on a multiplex bead array of 86 cytokine, chemokine, cytokine-receptor and immune-checkpoint antigens, and associations with best overall response and irAE development were assessed within pre-specified treatment strata by label-permutation testing with Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate control (SAM as a sensitivity analysis). Associations differed by ICI regimen. Anti-IL17A and anti-CCL2 reactivity was higher in patients developing irAEs under ipilimumab monotherapy (both p = 0.003) and shifted in the opposite direction under pembrolizumab without prior CTLA-4 therapy. Higher anti-PD-L1/CD274 and anti-CCL5 and lower anti-KIT reactivity were associated with response to pembrolizumab without prior CTLA-4 therapy (p = 0.025, p = 0.002, p = 0.006), and lower anti-MCAM and anti-CSF3 reactivity with response under ipilimumab/nivolumab (p = 0.001 and p = 0.002). No association survived false-discovery-rate correction, so all findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating; higher baseline anti-IL10 reactivity was a leading irAE signal under pembrolizumab without prior CTLA-4 therapy (p = 0.027). These regimen-dependent humoral markers warrant prospective, regimen-stratified validation.

papers.title: ENO1 Is More Abundant than ENO2 on the Surface of Metastatic and Neuroendocrine Prostate Cancer Cells and Upregulated in High-Risk Prostate Tumors.
papers.abstract: Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) remains lethal, and lineage plasticity drives a subset of tumors to neuroendocrine prostate cancer (NEPC), most often treatment-emergent (t-NEPC). Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA), the target of radioligand therapies for advanced prostate cancer (PCa), is heterogeneously expressed across metastatic sites but lost during neuroendocrine differentiation, excluding many patients from these therapies. The glycolytic enzyme Enolase 1 (ENO1) is a promising alternative target because it localizes to the surface of human tumors and promotes cancer growth and metastasis. However, it remains understudied in advanced PCa compared with ENO2 (neuron-specific enolase), a canonical neuroendocrine marker. We report here that total and cell surface ENO1 are more abundant than ENO2 in PSMA-negative mCRPC and NEPC cells. ENO1 silencing reduced cell proliferation and clonogenic growth even when triggering ENO2 upregulation. Targeting cell surface ENO1 with a monoclonal antibody decreased proliferation, clonogenicity, and tumorsphere formation in mCRPC cells, including docetaxel-resistant cells. This was associated with S-phase accumulation, elevated phospho histone p-H2A.X, and increased apoptosis. Significantly higher transcript expression of ENO1 than ENO2 was observed in clinical prostate tumors, including high-Gleason and neuroendocrine tumors, concomitant with elevated expression of their transcriptional regulator MYC. These findings position cell-surface ENO1 as a therapeutic and theranostic target for PSMA-low, treatment-refractory PCa.

papers.title: Carcinoembryonic Antigen (CEA) as a Therapeutic Target in Medullary Thyroid Cancer (MTC).
papers.abstract: Medullary thyroid cancer (MTC) is a rare but aggressive neuroendocrine malignancy arising from parafollicular C cells. Despite its low incidence, MTC has historically been estimated to account for 13.4% of thyroid cancer-related deaths. Survival outcomes remain limited in advanced disease, with a historical cohort reporting a 10-year survival of 21% for stage IV MTC, supporting the need for novel therapeutic approaches. Carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA), a fetal glycoprotein minimally expressed in normal adult tissues, is elevated in various malignancies and plays an established role in carcinogenesis, metastasis, and therapy resistance. In MTC, CEA is produced by neoplastic C cells alongside calcitonin, and both serum and tumor-associated CEA levels are markedly elevated relative to healthy tissue. More than half of MTC patients demonstrate elevated CEA, and intense CEA immunohistochemical staining correlates with aggressive, disseminated disease, highlighting its potential utility as both a biomarker and investigational therapeutic target in the disease. For MTC, surgery is the mainstay for locoregional disease with the intent for complete surgical resection when possible. Systemic therapy is generally reserved for structurally progressive, unresectable, symptomatic, or threatening advanced disease, with selective RET inhibitors used in RET-mutant disease and multi-kinase TKIs as additional treatment options. Although TKIs have improved progression-free survival, treatment can be limited by toxicities and the development of resistance over time. These limitations underscore the need for novel therapeutic strategies that can achieve more durable disease control and improve overall survival. Given its strong association with tumor burden, disease progression, and aggressive pathology, CEA represents a promising investigational target for therapeutic exploration in MTC. A narrative literature review was performed to evaluate carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) as a therapeutic target and biomarker in medullary thyroid cancer (MTC). Searches were conducted in 2025 and 2026 using PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Library, Scopus, Web of Science, and ClinicalTrials.gov. The current literature supports further investigation of CEA targeting as a therapeutic strategy in MTC. However, CEA is not yet a clinically validated therapeutic target and clinical trial data remain limited.

papers.title: Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio as a Prognostic Biomarker in Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Neoplasms.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms (PNENs) represent a rare, heterogeneous group of tumors with highly variable clinical outcomes. While standard clinicopathological parameters like World Health Organization (WHO) grading and TNM staging provide critical prognostic data, they do not fully explain the survival disparities observed in patients with similar tumor characteristics. This narrative review evaluates the clinical and prognostic significance of the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR)-a widely accessible marker of systemic inflammation-in patients with PNENs. A comprehensive literature review was conducted to synthesize current evidence regarding the prognostic utility of peripheral NLR levels. Studies conducted specifically in pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (PNETs) suggest that elevated peripheral blood NLR is associated with adverse clinicopathological features and, in several cohorts, with shorter overall survival (OS) and recurrence-free survival (RFS). However, the strength and independence of these associations vary across studies. Evidence from mixed gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasm (GEP-NEN) cohorts undergoing systemic treatment or peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) provides complementary insights into the predictive capacity of NLR regarding treatment response, though it remains indirect evidence for PNETs, particularly when pancreatic-specific subgroup results are unavailable. Differences in tumor differentiation, grade, stage, treatment setting, and NLR cut-off values limit direct comparisons across studies. NLR is an accessible, candidate adjunctive prognostic biomarker in PNETs, particularly in surgically treated populations. However, the evidence remains highly heterogeneous, and its clinical utility and standardized thresholds remain unvalidated. Proposed applications in treatment selection or surveillance intensity should be strictly regarded as investigational and hypothesis-generating, rather than validated clinical strategies. NLR should complement, rather than replace, established clinicopathological prognostic factors.

papers.title: Risk factors for postoperative hyponatremia after endoscopic endonasal surgery for nonfunctioning pituitary adenoma.
papers.abstract: Postoperative hyponatremia is a common complication after endoscopic endonasal surgery (EES) for pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (Pit-NETs, also known as a pituitary adenoma), but its underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study evaluated its incidence, clinical course, and risk factors after EES for nonfunctioning pituitary adenoma/ Pit-NET. We retrospectively reviewed 229 patients who underwent EES for nonfunctioning pituitary adenomas/ Pit-NETs between April 2014 and March 2024. Postoperative hyponatremia was defined as serum sodium < 135 mEq/L. Clinical, radiological, endocrine, and perioperative variables, including body mass index (BMI), tumor dimensions, and intraoperative cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leakage graded using the Esposito classification, were analyzed. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify risk factors. Postoperative hyponatremia occurred in 36 patients (15.7%) at a mean of 6.6 ± 1.9 days after surgery. Fluid restriction alone achieved sodium normalization in 31 patients (86.1%). Univariate analysis identified lower BMI, Esposito grade 3 CSF leakage, and larger superior-inferior tumor diameter as significant risk factors. Multivariate analysis revealed that lower BMI (p = 0.021; odds ratio [OR] 0.873; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.778-0.979) and Esposito grade 3 (p = 0.049; OR, 3.251; 95% CI, 1.006-10.50) were independently associated with postoperative hyponatremia. Lower BMI and Esposito grade 3 CSF leakage were independent risk factors for postoperative hyponatremia after EES for nonfunctioning pituitary adenomas/ Pit-NETs. These findings may help identify patients requiring careful postoperative sodium monitoring.

papers.title: Intraoperative technology in skull base and vascular neurosurgery: a two-stage cross-sectional national survey.
papers.abstract: Skull base and vascular neurosurgery rely on diverse intraoperative technologies, but contemporary data describing how frequently they are used at the level of individual operations are limited. On behalf of the Society of British Neurological Surgeons (SBNS) MedTech Committee, we aimed to establish a dated descriptive baseline of reported technology use across three operative paradigms. We conducted a two-stage cross-sectional survey of neurosurgeons in the UK and Ireland via the Society of British Neurological Surgeons (SBNS). Six MedTech Committee members compiled a pragmatic technology list. Respondents reported frequency of use for three exemplar procedures: transsphenoidal pituitary adenoma, retrosigmoid vestibular schwannoma, and pterional aneurysm surgery. Use was recorded on a four-point ordinal scale and analysed descriptively, with Kendall's tau-b used to explore the relationship between experience and reported use. Twenty-four responses from 20 of the 32 adult or mixed adult-paediatric UK units were analysed (11 units per index procedure). Reported use was strongly procedure specific. Neuronavigation was used always or almost always by 8/12 transsphenoidal respondents but infrequently elsewhere. Endoscopy had displaced microscopy in transsphenoidal surgery, whereas microscopy was used always or almost always by all retrosigmoid and pterional respondents. Indocyanine green and micro-Doppler were routine for aneurysms. Neurophysiological monitoring was universal for vestibular schwannoma but evenly divided for aneurysms. Exoscopes, intraoperative MRI and robotics were used infrequently or not at all; augmented reality was reported by 5/13 pterional respondents. No association was found between experience and reported use, though this was underpowered. Reported intraoperative technology use is strongly shaped by operative paradigm, with established technologies clustering around recurring procedural needs. Newer technologies were used infrequently. Because availability was not recorded, non-use cannot be distinguished from lack of access. These data provide a dated baseline against which future change can be assessed.

papers.title: Electrospun Polyvinylpyrrolidone Fibrous Membranes Loaded With Sanghuangporus sanghuang Ethanol Extract: In Vitro Release and Inhibitory Effects on B16-F10 Melanoma Cells.
papers.abstract: Sanghuangporus sanghuang ethanol extract (SSEE) is rich in flavonoids and polyphenols, showing antitumor potential. However, poor solubility and low delivery efficiency limit its clinical use. This study loaded SSEE into polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) via electrospinning to prepare composite fibrous membranes. The composite fibers exhibited distinct release profiles of total phenolic compounds under the tested conditions. All tested fibrous membranes exhibited low cytotoxicity toward human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs), while the SSEE/PVP fibrous membranes achieved proliferation inhibition rates of over 70% against B16-F10 melanoma cells. SSEE-containing treatments markedly reduced scratch wound closure in B16-F10 cells. Preliminary network pharmacology analysis suggested potential involvement of the phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)-Akt and mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling pathways, warranting further investigation. In conclusion, SSEE/PVP fibrous membranes exhibited promising in vitro inhibitory effects on B16-F10 melanoma cells. Network pharmacology suggested that the PI3K‑Akt/MAPK axis and inflammation‑apoptosis pathways may be involved, warranting further validation. SSEE/PVP fibrous membranes show potential as a local delivery system for SSEE-derived components.

papers.title: Early-onset pancreatic malignancies in São Paulo, Brazil: histology, treatment patterns, and survival in a hospital-based registry of 17,374 patients.
papers.abstract: Early-onset cancers are increasing at several gastrointestinal sites, but pancreatic tumors diagnosed before age 50 are poorly characterized in Latin America. We compared histology, treatment, and survival by age at diagnosis in São Paulo, Brazil. We analyzed pancreatic neoplasms (ICD-O C25) registered in the São Paulo State Hospital-Based Cancer Registry, 2000-2025. Early onset was defined as age <50 years. Histology was classified by four-digit ICD-O morphology. Cox models adjusted for covariates known at diagnosis; treatment was assessed as a time-dependent covariate and in three-month landmark analyses. Temporal trends in early-onset share were modeled by binomial regression. Among 17,374 patients, 2477 (14.3%) had early-onset disease. Compared with later-onset cases, these more often involved the body or tail (22.1% vs 17.2%), neuroendocrine histology (22.4% vs 6.8%), or solid pseudopapillary histology (5.9% vs 0.3%); surgery was also more often recorded (46.3% vs 29.1%; all p < 0.001). Median survival was 13.1 versus 5.5 months. The adjusted hazard ratio (HR) was 0.79 (95% CI 0.74-0.83) and remained 0.79 (0.75-0.84) with time-dependent treatment. The age term departed from proportional hazards; the unadjusted 60-month restricted mean survival difference was 11.4 months. Subgroup HRs (95% CIs) were 0.83 (0.78-0.88) for ductal adenocarcinoma and 0.68 (0.57-0.81) for neuroendocrine neoplasms (interaction ratio 0.82, 95% CI 0.69-0.99; p = 0.039). The early-onset share declined annually (OR 0.981, 95% CI 0.975-0.988). Early-onset neoplasms were enriched for neuroendocrine and solid pseudopapillary tumors and associated with better adjusted survival, although residual confounding remains possible.

papers.title: A Structured Workflow for Four-Plex Chromogenic Immunohistochemistry Panel Design, Validation, and Digital Imaging for Immune Cell Quantification.
papers.abstract: To support immune profiling of solid tumors using brightfield microscopy and digital image analysis, this study aims to develop an analytically validated workflow to design and implement a four-plex chromogenic IHC panel targeting CD8, CD20, CD68, and pan-cytokeratin. We developed a stepwise approach combining antibody optimization, chromogen selection, and qualitative evaluation using microscopy, digital image analysis, and red-green-blue histograms (RGB). After testing 15 dual-stain combinations and three four-plex panel designs, we found that the panel comprising CD8-DAB, CD20-Teal, CD68-Purple, and pan-cytokeratin-Yellow provided optimal stain separation and consistent performance. Using this approach, we established a reliable and effective method to analyze immune cell densities in solid tumors. This panel was validated across 12 solid tumor types, including carcinomas, neuroendocrine neoplasms, and sarcomas, demonstrating consistent efficacy in quantifying immune cell densities. Our study presents a structured validation workflow for brightfield multiplex immunohistochemistry panel design and digital image analysis integration. The validated four-plex panel enabled accurate immune profiling across tumor types and was compatible with standard pathology procedures, supporting its utility in translational research and its potential for future clinical implementation.

papers.title: Fight or Flight: A Multidisciplinary Approach to Diagnosis and Management of Mediastinal Paragangliomas.
papers.abstract: Mediastinal paragangliomas are rare neuroendocrine tumors, leading to potentially invasive clinical investigation and inadequate staging. Functional secretory activity, high germline mutation rates, multifocal disease burden, and proximity to the great vessels demand a multidisciplinary approach. We describe our longitudinal multidisciplinary experience building a center of excellence model. We performed a retrospective single-center cohort study of 19 patients with mediastinal paraganglioma managed at a quaternary referral center, capturing demographics, imaging, preoperative testing, operative details, and perioperative outcomes. There were 14 (73.7%) females with a median age of 46.3 years (IQR 38.5-57.6 years). Sixteen (84%) of 19 patients were referred from outside centers; 9 (47.3%) underwent biopsy before referral, with three (15.8%) experiencing catecholamine crisis, pneumothorax, or hemorrhage. Nine (47.4%) tumors were adjacent to the aorta, and seven (42.1%) adjacent to the pulmonary artery, with vascular involvement in 17(89.5%) of the 19 patients. Thirteen (68%) were functional and five (26.3%) had multifocal disease. Succinate dehydrogenase mutations were found in 63.6% of patients tested. Cardiopulmonary bypass was required in 63.2%, with zero 30-day mortality. Postoperative complications occurred in 47.4%, predominantly atrial arrhythmia. Median hospital stay was four days. Four patients developed local recurrence at a median recurrence-free survival of 16.9 months, all with positive margins or multifocal disease. Mediastinal paragangliomas can be safely resected within a multidisciplinary center of excellence. Early recognition, avoidance of uninformed biopsy, functional staging, preoperative alpha blockade, and tumor profiling and genetic evaluation with genetic counseling are essential components.

papers.title: Treatment with [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE in patients with neuroendocrine tumors at high risk of carcinoid crisis: a multidisciplinary clinical protocol.
papers.abstract: Therapy with [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE is an established treatment for patients with well-differentiated, unresectable or metastatic neuroendocrine tumors expressing somatostatin receptors. In patients with functioning tumors and carcinoid syndrome, radiopharmaceutical administration may trigger a carcinoid crisis, an uncommon, but potentially severe, complication. This article presents a multidisciplinary clinical protocol for the identification, preparation, treatment, and follow-up of patients at high risk of carcinoid crisis during [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE therapy. The protocol is based on the evidence available and our institutional clinical experience. It describes risk criteria, pretreatment assessment, optimization of carcinoid syndrome, the inpatient clinical care pathway, the therapeutic procedure, crisis management, nursing care, radiation protection, and radioactive waste management. The protocol aims to reduce variability in clinical practice, facilitate early recognition of carcinoid crisis, and establish a safe and reproducible care pathway for patients and healthcare professionals.

papers.title: Long-term disease control in Knosp grade 4 Cushing's disease using maximal safe resection and early adjuvant radiotherapy.
papers.abstract: Knosp grade 4 Cushing's disease (CD) represents an anatomically extreme and clinically challenging subtype of pituitary neuroendocrine tumor because a lesion extending deeply lateral to the intracavernous internal carotid artery (ICA) is rarely amenable to complete and safe resection via transsphenoidal surgery. Persistent hypercortisolism in CD directly compromises long-term survival, while aggressive lateral cavernous sinus (CS) dissection carries substantial neurovascular risk. Dedicated outcome studies focusing exclusively on Knosp grade 4 CD remain scarce. Therefore, the authors evaluated the long-term outcomes of a treatment strategy combining maximal safe resection with early adjuvant radiotherapy (RT) for residual CS disease while intentionally avoiding excessively aggressive lateral CS dissection beyond the ICA. The authors retrospectively reviewed the records of consecutive patients with biochemically confirmed CD and Knosp grade 4 CS invasion treated between 2009 and 2025. The surgical strategy prioritized maximal safe tumor resection while avoiding excessively aggressive dissection lateral to the ICA. Early adjuvant stereotactic RT was administered for residual lateral CS disease. Clinical, endocrinological, and radiological outcomes were analyzed during long-term follow-up, and factors potentially associated with poor disease control were explored. Thirty patients were included in the analysis. Endocrinological and radiological disease control was achieved in 26 (87%) of them during a mean follow-up of 70.5 months. Tumor progression occurred in 4 patients, all of whom demonstrated persistent hypercortisolism, and 3 subsequently died of disease-related causes. Prior RT exposure and an elevated Ki-67 labeling index were associated with poorer disease control despite multimodal treatment including temozolomide. In contrast, durable endocrine control was achieved in all Crooke cell adenoma cases under the described treatment strategy. No patient experienced ICA injury or disabling cranial neuropathy attributable to aggressive lateral CS dissection. For Knosp grade 4 CD, durable endocrine control must be balanced against the risks of radical CS surgery. Maximal safe resection combined with early adjuvant RT for residual CS disease provided favorable long-term disease control while avoiding major surgical morbidity. These findings support planned early adjuvant RT as a reasonable strategy for residual lateral CS disease in this rare and anatomically extreme subtype.

papers.title: The multifaceted expression of the gastrin releasing peptide receptor in prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: Gastrin releasing peptide receptor (GRPR) gained interest for targeted radionuclide therapy (TRT) of prostate cancer (PCa). However, its expression in advanced disease remains understudied. We correlated clinical, biological, molecular and pathological characteristics, with GRPR expression in PCa patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models, and compared it with prostate specific membrane antigen (PSMA) expression. GRPR expression was studied on tissue microarrays of 107 PDXs using immunohistochemistry. Seventy-six samples were GRPR positive. There were no differences in GRPR expression between primary and metastatic lesions, and androgen-naïve, androgen sensitive and castration resistant samples. High GRPR expression was frequent in androgen receptor (AR) positive tumors, high PSMA-expressing tumors, tumors without phosphatase and tensin homolog (PTEN) loss, and vimentin negative tumors. AR-positivity was the most important predictor of high GRPR expression. In PSMA negative tumors, GRPR expression was high in chromogranin positive tumors, tumors without PTEN loss, in absence of retinoblastoma1-gene mutation, and high vimentin-expressing tumors. Among the neuroendocrine PCa's (NEPC), 14/20 were GRPR and 3/20 were PSMA positive. All PSMA positive tumors were GRPR positive. Among metastatic NEPC samples, 9/10 and 1/10 were GRPR and PSMA positive, respectively. Based on the aforementioned, we conclude that GRPR is a relevant target for advanced PCa. Moreover, the selective GRPR expression in NEPC opens new avenues for GRPR-TRT. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-64701-7.

papers.title: When hypertensive crisis mimics septic shock: A case report of pheochromocytoma-induced severe lactic acidosis following GLP-1 receptor agonist administration.
papers.abstract: Pheochromocytoma is a rare catecholamine-secreting tumor that may present atypically with severe lactic acidosis and systemic inflammatory features, closely mimicking sepsis and delaying diagnosis. A possible interaction with glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists has been suggested but remains poorly understood. A 48-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus presented with acute nausea, vomiting, chills, severe abdominal pain, and hypertensive crisis within hours of self-administering tirzepatide, a dual GLP-1/glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor agonist. She was febrile, tachycardic, and markedly hypertensive, with severe lactic acidosis and systemic inflammatory markers suggestive of sepsis. Initial evaluation favored sepsis; however, negative cultures, sustained severe hypertension, hyperlactatemia disproportionate to perfusion status, and elevated urinary normetanephrines redirected the evaluation toward an endocrine cause. The clinical and biochemical picture supported a diagnosis of probable pheochromocytoma. Imaging revealed a fat-containing left adrenal mass initially suggestive of myelolipoma, representing a diagnostic pitfall. The patient was managed with intravenous fluids, a continuous nicardipine infusion, and oral alpha-blockade with doxazosin. Empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics were started and later discontinued as infection became unlikely. Beta-blockade was withheld until adequate alpha-blockade was achieved. Supportive care and electrolyte correction were provided. Blood pressure and lactate improved over 48 hours with clinical stabilization. The patient was discharged on oral alpha-blockade with plans for outpatient functional imaging (64Cu-DOTATATE positron emission tomography) and definitive surgical evaluation. Pheochromocytoma should be considered in patients presenting with unexplained lactic acidosis and hypertensive crisis, even when sepsis appears likely. Catecholamine-driven type B lactic acidosis can closely mimic infectious shock. Fat-containing adrenal lesions do not exclude pheochromocytoma, and biopsy should be avoided. The temporal association with GLP-1 receptor agonist exposure is hypothesis-generating and warrants further investigation as use of these agents continues to expand.

papers.title: Minimally invasive removal of intradural extramedullary tumor using unilateral biportal endoscopic technique: A technical case report.
papers.abstract: Intradural extramedullary (IDEM) tumors are mostly benign spinal lesions but may lead to progressive neurological symptoms due to spinal cord or nerve root compression. The unilateral biportal endoscopic (UBE) technique, widely used in spinal decompression and fusion, has rarely been applied to intradural pathologies. This case report presents a case of IDEM tumor resection using the UBE technique. A 50-year-old man presented with a 2-month history of low back pain and 1 month of left leg numbness. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed an IDEM tumor at the T9-T10 level, suggestive of a schwannoma. The patient underwent tumor resection using a UBE technique. The dura was closed using a continuous 4-0 barbed suture under endoscopic visualization. The procedure lasted 7.8 hours, with an estimated blood loss of 200 mL. The postoperative hospital stay was 6 days, and no cerebrospinal fluid leakage occurred. Histopathological examination confirmed a benign schwannoma. The patient's symptoms resolved completely without neurological deficits. Follow-up magnetic resonance imaging at 6 months showed no evidence of recurrence. This case report presents the use of the UBE technique for IDEM tumor resection in a selected patient, with satisfactory surgical outcomes.

papers.title: Systemic purinergic dysregulation in melanoma revealed by soluble P2RX4 receptor fragments.
papers.abstract: Melanoma progression involves coordinated immune suppression, altered receptor-mediated signalling, and tumour-driven metabolic reprogramming. To evaluate these systemic alterations, we integrated three datasets: flow-cytometric profiling of immune cell subsets and P2X4R expression in peripheral blood leukocytes from melanoma patients and healthy controls; molecular detection of P2X4R in plasma, leukocytes, and urine using Western blotting and immunoprecipitation; and NMR-based metabolomic profiling of serum and saliva. Melanoma patients exhibited reduced CD4⁺ T-helper cells, altered Tc/Treg balance, and eosinophil heterogeneity with elevated P2X4R expression. Truncated P2X4R fragments were detected in plasma and urine of some melanoma patients but not in controls. Metabolomic analyses revealed tumour-associated metabolic shifts, including elevated branched-chain amino acids in both serum and saliva as well as multiple alterations associated with dysbiosis were detected in melanoma patients' saliva. These findings demonstrate parallel alterations in immune composition, P2X4-associated purinergic signalling, and systemic metabolism in melanoma. The presence of soluble P2X4R fragments, together with metabolomic fingerprints, supports their potential as minimally invasive biomarkers for disease monitoring.

papers.title: Cystic pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors: a practical imaging approach.
papers.abstract: Cystic pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (c-PanNETs) are an uncommon cystic phenotype of well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, accounting for approximately 7-12% of PanNETs in several surgical series, although reported frequencies vary according to the definition of cystic morphology and cohort selection. Retrospective studies suggest that c-PanNETs may exhibit less aggressive clinicopathologic features than their solid counterparts; however, their imaging appearance frequently overlaps with other pancreatic cystic neoplasms, particularly branch-duct intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms, mucinous cystic neoplasms, and atypical serous cystic neoplasms. Accurate preoperative recognition may have important implications for patient management and surgical planning. This review summarizes the imaging features of c-PanNETs across computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, and magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography, as well as the complementary roles of endoscopic ultrasound and somatostatin receptor PET/CT. Particular attention is given to arterial hyperenhancement of the cyst wall, septations, mural nodules, or residual solid components; assessment of communication with the main pancreatic duct; and integration of complementary imaging findings. Because these features are not specific, their interpretation in combination with lesion morphology and ductal relationships is emphasized. Practical approaches to differential diagnosis and common interpretive pitfalls are also discussed. The review further addresses emerging quantitative imaging techniques, including radiomics and artificial intelligence, while recognizing that evidence specific to c-PanNETs remains limited. A practical diagnostic algorithm and structured reporting checklist are provided to support systematic interpretation and multidisciplinary communication. Recognition of the imaging spectrum of c-PanNETs, combined with systematic assessment of enhancement characteristics, ductal anatomy, and complementary imaging findings, may improve diagnostic confidence and support appropriate patient management.

papers.title: Immune Subtypes of PPGL: Genomic Determinants and Therapeutic Implications.
papers.abstract: Pheochromocytomas and paragangliomas (PPGLs) are rare neuroendocrine neoplasms with significant hereditary predisposition and metastatic potential for which systemic treatment options remain limited. Although characterized as immunologically inert tumors, emerging evidence reveals a biologically meaningful diversity of immune subtypes whose distribution is tightly coupled to genomic subtype, metabolic phenotype, and clinical behavior. PPGLs are classified into three major transcriptional clusters, pseudohypoxic, kinase signaling, and WNT-altered, each associated with a characteristic tumor microenvironment (TME). Pseudohypoxic tumors, driven by SDHx and related alterations, display immunosuppressive microenvironments enriched in fibroblast-like perivascular cells and shaped by succinate accumulation and HIF-2α-mediated signaling, while kinase signaling tumors preferentially associate with immune-enriched profiles. MAML3 fusion-positive tumors represent a distinct immunological exception, combining adaptive PD-L1 overexpression with CD8+ T cell and NK cell infiltration and a higher predicted neoantigen burden, whose functional relevance remains to be established. Secondary genomic events, particularly ATRX mutations, TERT activation, and somatic copy number alterations, further modulate immune contexture and metastatic risk. Pan-cancer immune classification frameworks identify lymphocyte-depleted subtypes as predominant in PPGLs, with a progressive shift toward greater immunosuppression in metastatic disease. These findings have direct therapeutic implications: the HIF-2α inhibitor belzutifan has demonstrated meaningful activity in pseudohypoxic tumors and may carry immunomodulatory effects, while MAML3 fusion-positive and immune-enriched kinase signaling tumors may represent the subset most amenable to immune checkpoint inhibition. Translating this biological complexity into clinical benefit will require molecularly stratified trials, standardized immune profiling, and expanded international collaborative efforts.

papers.title: 2026 ETA Consensus Statement on the Interpretation and Management of Calcitonin Levels in Patients with Thyroid Nodules.
papers.abstract: Calcitonin (Ctn) is widely recognized as the most accurate test for the early detection of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC). Nevertheless, universal agreement on whether to routinely measure serum Ctn in all patients with thyroid nodules has not been achieved, mainly due to the perceived limited cost-effectiveness, the strict preanalytical workup needed for Ctn measurements, and the difficulties in interpreting borderline or mildly elevated Ctn concentrations in the presence of not fully interchangeable Ctn immunoassays. Although MTC is a rare malignancy, its prognosis is strongly dependent on the stage at diagnosis, that is strictly correlated to Ctn levels that reflect both the presence and burden of MTC. For these reasons the interpretation of preoperative Ctn concentrations, whenever performed, is critically important. This consensus aims to support clinicians who perform Ctn in the work up of thyroid nodules, either routinely or in accordance to the ETA guidelines, in decision-making when Ctn concentrations are above the upper reference limit, but not yet approaching or reaching the diagnostic levels, by identifying those who require surgery, those suitable for follow-up, and those who do not require further investigation.

papers.title: Recurrent Hypertensive Carcinoid Crisis Despite Somatostatin Analog Therapy.
papers.abstract: Carcinoid crisis is a rare, life-threatening complication of neuroendocrine tumors characterized by hemodynamic instability. Although hypotension is more commonly described, severe hypertension can also occur. An 84-year-old woman who had undergone resection of a grade 1 terminal ileal neuroendocrine tumor and two hepatic metastases presented with worsening flushing, severe headaches, mild wheeze, palpitations, and chest tightness. She was receiving maintenance long-acting lanreotide and had used the maximum prescribed dose of rescue subcutaneous octreotide for two weeks without sustained benefit. Her blood pressure was highly labile, with a peak systolic reading of 198 mmHg, and her heart rate reached 110 beats/min. The endocrinology team diagnosed a hypertensive carcinoid crisis. Her symptoms and hypertension resolved within 24 h of commencing a continuous intravenous octreotide infusion, and a plan was made to shorten the lanreotide dosing interval from three weeks to two weeks. Eleven days after discharge, she was readmitted with recurrent flushing, palpitations, tachycardia, and hypertension after the dose due under the revised lanreotide schedule was delayed. Subcutaneous octreotide improved the flushing and hypertension, while bisoprolol was introduced for persistent symptomatic tachycardia. Cardiac investigations showed no sustained arrhythmia or major structural abnormality. Biochemical markers measured after treatment were within their reference ranges. Subsequent somatostatin receptor positron emission tomography/computed tomography demonstrated new receptor-avid disease in the liver and left pelvis that had not been identified on preceding conventional imaging. This case demonstrates that hypertension can be the predominant hemodynamic manifestation of carcinoid crisis and highlights the limited value of normal biomarkers obtained after somatostatin analog treatment, which should not be used in isolation to exclude an acute crisis.

papers.title: The Evolving Role of Endoscopy in Gastric and Duodenal Neuroendocrine Tumors.
Metabolic Flexibility of Cutaneous Melanoma Cells Upon Autophagy Modulation: An Immunohistochemical Study.
papers.abstract: Autophagy plays a complex and multifaceted role in melanoma, acting both as a tumor suppressor and as a mechanism supporting tumor cell survival. The metabolic plasticity of tumor cells is closely interconnected with autophagic processes. Despite several therapeutic advances with autophagy-modulating agents, this field remains insufficiently explored. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effects of autophagy modulators (lithium and chloroquine) on the metabolism of B16 murine melanoma cells. Both agents induced early apoptosis; however, necrosis predominated at the 24-hour time point. Studies in melanoma-bearing mice confirmed that chloroquine suppresses mitochondrial metabolism: expression of IDH3α was reduced twofold, whereas expression of the lactate transporter MCT4 was significantly increased. The mTOR/AKT and SMAD3 signaling pathways were differentially regulated: chloroquine reduced phospho-mammalian target of rapamycin (ph-mTOR) and SMAD3 expression yet increased total protein kinase B (AKT) levels, while lithium exerted a moderate effect on ph-mTOR. These findings suggest that chloroquine likely induces a metabolic shift toward glycolysis, whereas lithium helps maintain oxidative metabolism. The metabolic flexibility of tumor cells characterized in this study provides a strong rationale for combined therapeutic approaches for melanoma.

papers.title: Multiple co-occurring genetic variants in an elderly patient with Liddle's-like syndrome: a case report and literature review.
papers.abstract: Liddle syndrome (LS) is a rare autosomal dominant condition classically defined by early-onset hypertension, hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis, and a suppressed renin-aldosterone profile, primarily driven by gain-of-function mutations in the SCNN1A, SCNN1B, or SCNN1G genes encoding the epithelial sodium channel (ENaC). Nevertheless, genetically investigated cases exhibiting Liddle's-like phenotypes in the elderly population remain exceptionally rare. We report a 61-year-old male admitted with recurrent limb weakness and resistant hypertension. A comprehensive clinical workup, including biochemical profiles, RAAS evaluation, and 24-h ABPM, was conducted to exclude common secondary causes. Following informed consent, whole-exome sequencing (WES) was performed, with candidate variants validated by Sanger sequencing and assessed per ACMG/AMP guidelines. To guide therapeutic management, a narrative literature review of similar cases was also performed searching PubMed, Web of Science, and CNKI using keywords like "Liddle syndrome," "elderly," "hypertension," and "hypokalemia.". Admission tests showed hypokalemia (2.94 mmol/L), compensated metabolic alkalosis, and suppressed renin-aldosterone levels. 24-h ABPM indicated severe blood pressure fluctuations up to 185/120 mmHg. Genetic testing revealed three heterozygous variants of uncertain significance (VUS)-CYP3A5 (c.1253 + 83C > T), SCNN1G (c.1727A > G, p.Lys576Arg), and WNK1 (c.5636A > T, p.Asp1879Val)-without any known pathogenic variants. A diagnostic trial with triamterene (50 mg twice daily) restored normal potassium levels (> 3.5 mmol/L). After a 30-day combination therapy of controlled-release nifedipine and irbesartan, blood pressure stabilized between 110 and 133 and 69-85 mmHg. We report an elderly patient with chronic hypokalemia and resistant hypertension. After ruling out common secondary causes (for example, primary aldosteronism, Cushing's syndrome, pheochromocytoma), Liddle's-like syndrome was clinically diagnosed based on the low-renin/low-aldosterone biochemical phenotype, compensated metabolic alkalosis, literature review, and a selective response to triamterene. This case suggests that Liddle's-like syndrome must be considered in the differential diagnosis of hypokalemic hypertension in older adults to ensure early and targeted therapy.

papers.title: Recurrent intraoperative asystole induced by tumor manipulation in a cervical vagal schwannoma: a case report.
papers.abstract: Vagal schwannomas are rare, benign tumors arising from Schwann cells of the vagus nerve. Surgical resection is the mainstay of treatment but carries significant risks, including intraoperative hemodynamic instability due to vagal nerve manipulation and postoperative cranial nerve deficits. We report the case of a 37-year-old previously healthy male who presented with an incidentally discovered right-sided cervical mass during a routine health examination. Preoperative electrocardiogram and color Doppler echocardiography revealed no cardiac abnormalities. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed a "string-of-beads" lesion, measuring approximately 6.8 cm in length and 1.0 cm in maximum anteroposterior diameter, located posterior to the right common carotid artery, suggestive of a vagal schwannoma. The patient underwent complete microsurgical excision of the tumor. During dissection, three distinct episodes of complete cardiac asystole were observed on the monitor, each lasting approximately 3-4 s, with spontaneous recovery upon cessation of traction. No atropine or temporary pacemaker was administered. The tumor was completely resected under microscopic visualization with meticulous hemostasis. Postoperatively, the patient exhibited no hoarseness, dysphagia, or Horner's syndrome, and was discharged on postoperative day 4 with an uneventful recovery. Pathological examination confirmed the diagnosis of schwannoma. This case highlights that intraoperative cardiac asystole induced by vagal schwannoma manipulation can be managed safely with immediate cessation of traction and close monitoring, even without pharmacological or pacemaker intervention. The absence of neurological deficits postoperatively underscores the importance of meticulous microsurgical technique and the potential value of considering traction-induced bradycardia as a "physiological neuromonitoring" signal.
