When a PanNET Is Not a PanNET: Avoiding the Diagnostic Pitfalls of Peripancreatic Paraganglioma-A Case-Based Review.
papers.abstract: Paragangliomas are rare extra-adrenal neuroendocrine tumors, with pancreas involvement being extremely uncommon. Their clinical and radiologic similarity with other more common pancreatic neoplasms can cause diagnostic uncertainty. We present a 70-year-old man who presented with acute cholangitis, and a 4.4 cm pancreatic tail mass was found incidentally. Biopsy suggested a well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor. Despite imaging and biopsy, the diagnosis was made postoperatively with histopathology revealing a paraganglioma in the peripancreatic fat. This case and brief review highlights the limitations of current diagnostic modalities and the need for a comprehensive evaluation in distinguishing paragangliomas from pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, which is essential for surgery, genetic counseling, and long-term management.

papers.title: Altered Leptin Signalling in Adrenal Tumours - Preliminary Study.
papers.abstract: Leptin and its receptor (LepR) are implicated in tumour biology, but their role across adrenal diseases remains incompletely defined. This study characterised leptin and LepR immunoreactivity in adrenal pathologies and compared these findings with transcript-level data in adrenocortical carcinoma (ACC). Immunohistochemistry was performed on an adrenal tissue microarray including ACC, adrenocortical adenoma (ACA), pheochromocytoma, adrenal hyperplasia, and normal adrenal cortex. Automated digital image analysis quantified staining intensity and the proportion of positive cells. Public datasets were used to compare LEP mRNA expression between ACC and normal adrenal tissue, while exploratory analyses examined associations with sex and age. Leptin immunoreactivity in ACC was lower than in several benign and reference adrenal groups, depending on the quantification readout. ACC showed lower staining intensity than ACA, pheochromocytoma, adrenal hyperplasia, and cancer-adjacent tissue. The proportion of leptin-positive cells was lower in ACC than in normal cortex, cancer-adjacent tissue, adrenal hyperplasia, and pheochromocytoma, but not ACA. LepR staining intensity was lower in ACC than in ACA and pheochromocytoma, but not lower than in normal cortex or adrenal hyperplasia. LEP mRNA was lower in ACC than in normal adrenal tissue; however, expression was very low in both groups, and adipose-lineage content explained about half of the difference. Females showed higher leptin staining intensity than males. In ACC, the proportion of leptin-positive cells was inversely associated with age, whereas in normal cortex it was positively associated with age; LepR showed no sex effect. These findings indicate altered leptin-axis immunoreactivity in malignant adrenocortical disease. As whole tissue cores were analyzed without adjustment for adipose or stromal content, the results should be considered hypothesis-generating and require validation in prospectively characterized cohorts.

papers.title: Prognostic Factors in Lenvatinib-Treated Differentiated Thyroid Cancer: A Real-World Study with Extended Follow-Up.
papers.abstract: Lenvatinib is a standard first-line treatment for progressive radioiodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer (RAI-R DTC), but real-world outcomes over extended follow-up and prognostic factors remain insufficiently characterized. We retrospectively analyzed 97 patients with progressive RAI-R DTC treated with lenvatinib at a single institution between 2015 and 2024. Patients with anaplastic or medullary thyroid carcinoma and those treated for less than six months were excluded. Progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were evaluated using the Kaplan-Meier method, and prognostic factors were assessed using Cox proportional hazards models. Median age at treatment initiation was 68 years, and 38% of patients had bone metastases. With a median follow-up of 36 months, median PFS and OS were 25 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 21-31) and 59 months (95% CI, 45-82), respectively. The objective response rate was 58%, and the disease control rate was 97%. Multivariate analysis identified older age as an independent predictor of shorter PFS (Hazard ratio [HR] 1.34 per decade of age, p<0.01) and OS (HR 1.63 per decade of age, p<0.005). Bone metastasis was independently associated with worse OS (HR 2.25, p<0.05) but not PFS. Receiver operating characteristic analyses suggested age cutoffs of approximately 70 years. Bone metastasis was associated with significantly poorer OS among older patients. Lenvatinib provided durable disease control in patients with RAI-R DTC. Older age at treatment initiation and bone metastasis were independent determinants of survival and may help guide risk stratification and treatment timing in clinical practice.

papers.title: Outcomes and Prognostic Factors in Ectopic Cushing Syndrome: The Experience of Two Tertiary Referral Centers.
papers.abstract: Ectopic Cushing syndrome (ECS) is an uncommon cause of adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)-dependent Cushing syndrome associated with high morbidity and mortality. The aim of this study was to characterize patients with ECS and to identify potential prognostic factors associated with outcomes, including the clinical utility of serum inflammation-based scores (SIBS). A retrospective observational study of 30 patients with ECS managed at two tertiary endocrinology referral centers. Demographic, tumor-related, clinical, and biochemical variables at diagnosis were analyzed. SIBS (neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio [NLR], platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio [PLR], lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio, and systemic immune-inflammation index) were calculated from baseline laboratory parameters. Primary tumor sites were the lung (60%), pancreas (10%), thymus (3%), bladder (3%), adrenal gland (3%), and occult origin (20%). Metastatic disease was present in 65% of patients. Survival was markedly heterogeneous, with a median survival of 50.61 days. Tumor resection was associated with improved survival (HR = 0.225), whereas male sex (HR = 2.808), metastatic disease (HR = 15.82), ACTH (HR = 1.002), morning cortisol (HR = 1.023), and late-night cortisol concentrations (HR = 1.027) were associated with increased mortality risk. NLR positively correlated with ACTH (r = 0.575) and morning cortisol (r = 0.658), but none of the evaluated SIBS predicted survival. ECS is characterized by a heterogeneous clinical course and poor early survival. Male sex, metastatic disease, and severe hypercortisolism are adverse prognostic factors for overall survival, whereas surgical resection is associated with better outcomes. Hormonal status correlates with inflammatory indices, but the prognostic value of SIBS requires further investigation.

papers.title: TRIB2 supports a high glycolytic phenotype in melanoma cells.
papers.abstract: Metabolic adaptation is a crucial driver of melanoma progression and therapy resistance. The pseudokinase Tribbles homolog 2 (TRIB2) is highly expressed in melanoma and is associated with poor outcomes and treatment resistance. However, its specific role in the metabolic profile of melanoma cells remained unexplored. This study aimed to investigate the impact of TRIB2 on cellular metabolism, and its role in metabolic adaptation in melanoma. The study used UACC-62 human melanoma cells with high endogenous TRIB2 expression and isogenic TRIB2-knockout (KO) clones generated via CRISPR-Cas9. Cell proliferation was assessed using trypan blue exclusion assays under treatment with metabolic drugs including 2-deoxyglucose (2-DG), and dichloroacetate (DCA). Metabolic phenotypes were evaluated by measuring glucose consumption, lactate production, and real-time analysis of glycolytic flux (ECAR) and mitochondrial respiration (OCR) using a Seahorse bioanalyzer. Reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels were measured by dihydroethidium (DHE) fluorescence. Gene expression was analyzed by qPCR, and protein levels were determined by western blot. Citrate synthase activity was measured enzymatically. TRIB2-KO cells exhibited significantly reduced basal proliferation compared with wild-type (WT) cells. KO cells were also more sensitive to the glycolytic inhibitor 2-DG. Conversely, WT cells were more susceptible to DCA treatment. Metabolic analyses confirmed that TRIB2-KO cells had lower glucose consumption, lactate production, and glycolytic capacity than WT cells. Mitochondrial respiratory function and the protein levels of key respiratory complexes were unchanged. Despite the reduction in glycolytic activity, TRIB2 depletion did not increase mitochondrial respiratory capacity and was associated with elevated basal intracellular superoxide levels. Among the molecular alterations identified, PDK4 was consistently reduced at both the mRNA and protein levels, whereas citrate synthase activity was significantly decreased despite preserved protein abundance, indicating selective alterations in mitochondrial carbon metabolism. TRIB2 expression promotes a glycolytic phenotype and contributes to metabolic adaptation in melanoma. Loss of TRIB2 does not induce a metabolic shift towards oxidative phosphorylation but instead results in broader metabolic rewiring characterized by reduced glycolysis together with selective alterations in mitochondrial carbon metabolism. These findings identify the TRIB2-PDK4 axis as a previously unrecognized component of metabolic regulation in melanoma and provide a rationale for further investigating its therapeutic potential.

papers.title: Benchmarking cell segmentation in two Spatialomics platforms with open-source software.
papers.abstract: The in situ tissue microenvironment is a complex mixture of different cell types, microanatomic structures, and acellular matrix material. Further, disease perturbs the morphologies of these features significantly. Spatial proteomics utilizing optical or mass spectrometer imaging simultaneously detects expression and subcellular localization of many proteins. Accurate identification of heterogeneous, irregular, and tightly interdigitating cell boundaries is a crucial step for all downstream analyses, including cell phenotyping and cell-cell interaction networks. We describe a benchmarking approach for rapid assessment of segmentation algorithm performance in melanoma and breast cancer contexts using mass spectrometer and optical spatial omics imaging platforms. Comparison of cell segmentation by fourteen methods to pathologist ground-truth annotation with Jaccard pixel index and F1 object measurement identified Cellpose models that performed well across different tumor samples and data sources with minimal fine-tuning. Algorithms utilizing cell membrane and nuclear features demonstrated better performance in both tumor samples. This benchmarking approach is a rapid and effective method to assess performance of cell segmentation methods in different contexts for efficient algorithm selection and iterative model training. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-70919-2.

papers.title: Non-immune microenvironmental cues driving melanoma local invasion, migration, and invasive phenotype switching.
papers.abstract: Melanoma remains the deadliest form of skin cancer and continues to account for a disproportionate number of deaths worldwide. Although targeted therapies have markedly improved outcomes for subsets of patients, both de novo and acquired resistance remain major clinical challenges, particularly in tumors with restricted systemic therapeutic options. Central to melanoma progression, invasion, and metastasis is the tumor microenvironment (TME), which engages in dynamic and reciprocal crosstalk with melanoma cells across all disease stages. Here, we synthesize recent advances elucidating how non-immune components of the melanoma TME (including keratinocytes, fibroblasts, extracellular matrix, and adipocytes) mechanistically regulate tumor motility and local invasion. We highlight how biochemical, biomechanical, and metabolic cues cooperatively remodel melanoma invasive behavior. Finally, we review current clinical efforts targeting melanoma-TME interactions and discuss critical gaps that must be addressed to advance these strategies into durable clinical therapies.

papers.title: Lateral and suprasellar MRI anatomy in pituitary neuroendocrine tumor surgery: interobserver agreement and associations with resection and intraoperative CSF leakage.
papers.abstract: Lateral cavernous-sinus extension and suprasellar tumor-arachnoid anatomy are distinct but overlapping dimensions of pituitary neuroendocrine tumor (PitNET) surgery. We evaluated whether reader-concordant preoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) descriptors of these two axes show different associations with extent of resection and intraoperative cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leakage. In this single-center retrospective study, two blinded neurosurgeons independently assessed preoperative MRI of 53 patients: modified Knosp grade, suprasellar height, bowing index, infundibular deviation angle, and a study-specific tumor-arachnoid cleft grade. Exploratory analyses examined resection extent and Esposito-graded leakage (15 events), with post hoc adjustment for maximal tumor diameter. Intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) were 0.995-0.999 for continuous measures; cleft agreement was 53/53 and Knosp exact agreement 96.2%. Knosp grade was most strongly associated with non-total resection (area under the curve [AUC] 0.908; diameter-adjusted odds ratio [OR] 10.8 per SD, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.4-48.9) but not leakage (AUC 0.648). Suprasellar height (AUC 0.747) and cleft grade (AUC 0.740) showed stronger leakage associations; none of 16 patients with a wide cleft (> 2 mm) leaked. Cleft grade and height were strongly collinear (ρ=-0.81); the cleft-leakage association persisted after diameter adjustment (OR 0.43, 95% CI 0.19-0.93). Lateral and suprasellar MRI descriptors, concordant between two readers, showed different, partly overlapping operative associations. Modified Knosp grade related most strongly to resection, whereas suprasellar features, particularly the study-specific cleft grade, showed stronger exploratory associations with intraoperative leakage. The cleft finding is hypothesis-generating and requires prospective external validation; added value over height and the sellar barrier is unproven.

papers.title: CRTC1::TRIM11 fusion (CMTCT) tumor with novel presentation in the nasal cavity of three patients.
papers.abstract: CRTC1::TRIM11 cutaneous melanocytic tumors are a recently described uncommon entity almost exclusively reported as arising in the skin with fewer than 70 described cases and no dedicated reports of tumors arising in the sinonasal cavity (SNC). We identified 3 cases arising in the SNC with similar morphology and immunophenotype, all harboring CRTC1::TRIM11 fusion. We present the clinical, histological, immunophenotype, and molecular profile of these tumors and compare our tumors with those previously reported in the literature and provide practical guidance for evaluating tumors in the SNC with undifferentiated, neuroendocrine, or melanocytic phenotype. Formalin-fixed, paraffin embedded tissue sections of the patients' tumors were examined and compared with routinely stained sections and by immunohistochemistry. Whole exome/whole transcriptome sequencing revealing CRTC1::TRIM11 fusions in each case was performed at Caris® Life Sciences. The patients were 34, 48, and 69 years of age, 2 females and 1 male. All tumors originated in the nasal cavity and hard palate. Original diagnoses were S100-negative granular cell tumor, poorly differentiated carcinoma and mucosal melanoma. All tumors demonstrated highly cellular proliferations of round/ovoid cells arranged in vague organoid clusters. Individual cells had moderate eosinophilic granular cytoplasm and round nuclei containing dispersed and granular chromatin with visible nucleoli resembling neuroendocrine tumors. The neural markers synaptophysin and chromogranin were negative, however, tumors expressed PGP9.5 and NCAM in 2 cases. All cases expressed SOX10 in a diffuse fashion but negative for S100, Melan-A, HMB-45. CRTC1::TRIM11 fusion was detected in all cases. This recently described CRTC1::TRIM11 fusion-driven tumor almost exclusively described in cutaneous sites, hence the current designation as cutaneous melanocytic tumor with CRTC1::TRIM11 fusion (CMTCT), can arise in the nasal cavity and should be considered in the differential diagnoses of aggressive tumors with similar morphologies in the SNC that include mucosal melanoma, sinonasal undifferentiated carcinoma, and neuroectodermal and neuroendocrine carcinomas.

papers.title: Lysosome-Targeted Iridium(III)-BODIPY Conjugates with GSH-Activatable Reactive Oxygen Species Generation for Enhanced Photodynamic Immunotherapy of Melanoma.
papers.abstract: Melanoma represents a major clinical challenge due to its aggressive nature, high metastatic potential, and resistance to conventional therapies. Herein, we developed two near-infrared iridium(III)-BODIPY conjugates (BODIPY-1-Ir and BODIPY-2-Ir) for glutathione (GSH)-activated photodynamic immunotherapy. These conjugates function as lysosome-targeting photosensitizers that deplete intracellular GSH to disrupt redox balance and enhance reactive oxygen species generation with light irradiation. The phototoxicity further induces cascading dendritic cell maturation and tumor-associated macrophage reprogramming, promoting immunogenic cell death. Both in vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated their excellent biocompatibility, strong photodynamic anticancer efficiency, and significant tumor growth inhibition, highlighting their potential as promising candidates for melanoma treatment.

papers.title: Personalized dosimetry for targeted radionuclide therapy: initial clinical experience from a case series at a tertiary cancer center (King Hussein Cancer Center).
papers.abstract: Targeted radionuclide therapy (TRT) plays a pivotal role in managing differentiated thyroid cancer, neuroendocrine tumors, and metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Personalized dosimetry quantifies absorbed radiation doses to tumors and organs at risk (OARs), enabling treatment individualization, improved therapeutic outcomes, and reduced toxicity. This retrospective case series evaluated four patients treated at King Hussein Cancer Center (KHCC) between February 2024 and July 2025 with [131I]iodine, [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE, or [177Lu] Lu-prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA). Patients were selected based on oligometastatic disease, adequate radiotracer uptake on baseline imaging, eligibility for radionuclide therapy, and absence of treatment contraindications. Dosimetry followed the medical internal radiation dose (MIRD) methodology with multi-timepoint imaging. Volumes of interest were segmented manually on post-therapy single photon emission computed tomography/computed tomography (SPECT/CT), time-activity curves were generated, and residence times were computed to estimate absorbed doses for tumor lesions and OARs. Treatment response was assessed using serial imaging and biochemical markers. The cohort included two females (aged 9 and 45 years) and two males (aged 65 and 81 years). Substantial inter- and intra-patient variability in absorbed dose and response patterns was observed. The 45-year-old female received 180 mCi (6660 MBq) of [131I]iodine; skeletal metastases showed a broad dose range (~63-115 Gy), and the patient achieved a complete biochemical response. In the pediatric [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE case, the patient received 75 mCi (2775 MBq) during the third treatment cycle; lesion dose (~8.8 Gy) and renal exposure remained within safe limits, despite asymmetric renal involvement. The 81-year-old male received 100 mCi (3700 MBq) of [177Lu]Lu-PSMA; a low lesion dose (~0.5 Gy) was observed, correlating with limited clinical benefit. The 65-year-old male received five cycles of 200 mCi (7400 MBq) [177Lu]Lu-PSMA each; marked lesion-specific heterogeneity was observed, with high-dose lesions regressing, whereas persistent PSMA-avid lesions suggested resistance. Across all patients, OAR doses remained below safety thresholds. Personalized dosimetry is feasible in routine clinical practice and provides critical insights into dose-response relationships. It guides treatment optimization, identifies undertreated lesions, and helps maintain OAR safety, supporting its integration into TRT workflows to enhance therapeutic precision and outcomes.

papers.title: Hemodynamic Challenges After Paraganglioma Resection in Fontan-Palliated Adult With Fontan-Associated Liver Disease.
papers.abstract: Chronic hypoxemia in cyanotic congenital heart disease is associated with increased risk of pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma (PPGL), particularly among patients with single-ventricle physiology. A 26-year-old man with unbalanced atrioventricular septal defect and extracardiac Fontan palliation, and Fontan-associated liver disease presented with hypertensive crisis, with imaging evidence of PPGL. The patient underwent robotic right adrenalectomy and nodule resection complicated by high-volume chylous ascites for several weeks. Chronic hypoxemia in cyanotic congenital heart disease, particularly univentricular physiology, is a well-established driver of PPGL. Existing guidelines mandate preoperative α-blockade and volume expansion for functional PPGL, but this approach is not tailored to Fontan physiology. We present a rare case of operative disruption of retroperitoneal lymphatics superimposed on Fontan-associated systemic venous and lymphatic congestion. Right heart catheterization, cautious α-blockade with volume expansion, and multidisciplinary perioperative management are essential to balance catecholamine blockade against the risks of venous congestion, lymphatic failure, bleeding, and thrombosis.

papers.title: The dual role of skin-resident Tregs: balancing autoimmunity in vitiligo and immune evasion in melanoma.
papers.abstract: Skin-resident regulatory T cells (Tregs) are specialized tissue-resident lymphocytes essential for maintaining skin immune homeostasis and tolerance. However, their functional plasticity allows them to drive diametrically opposing clinical outcomes depending on the local microenvironment. This review comprehensively examines the dual and divergent roles of skin-resident Tregs in two immunologically distinct diseases: vitiligo and melanoma. In vitiligo, an autoimmune condition characterized by the destruction of epidermal melanocytes, quantitative Treg deficiencies, impaired skin homing via the CCL22/CCR4 axis, and phenotypic instability-shifting toward a dysfunctional, pro-inflammatory Th1-like state-precipitate the breakdown of self-tolerance. This permits unrestrained autoreactive CD8+ cytotoxic T cell activity. Conversely, in melanoma, the tumor microenvironment (TME) actively recruits and metabolically reprograms Tregs into a highly suppressive state. These intratumoral Tregs upregulate inhibitory receptors (e.g., TIM-3, PD-1, CTLA-4) and secrete potent immunosuppressive cytokines, facilitating immune evasion by exhausting anti-tumor effector responses. By dissecting the mechanistic parallels and critical differences in Treg trafficking, phenotypic plasticity, and metabolic adaptation, this review provides a unified framework for understanding context-dependent immune regulation. Furthermore, we highlight emerging disease-specific therapeutic strategies, emphasizing approaches to replenish and enhance Treg function to restore immune tolerance in vitiligo, while selectively depleting or functionally impairing intratumoral Tregs to unleash anti-tumor immunity in melanoma.

papers.title: Ruptured pheochromocytoma during preoperative doxazosin treatment.
papers.abstract: Rupture of pheochromocytoma is rare but represents a life-threatening complication. A 43-year-old man with episodic hypertension, palpitations, and chest discomfort was incidentally found, during a computed tomography (CT) aortogram performed to rule out aortic dissection, to have a 5.2-cm right adrenal mass suspicious for pheochromocytoma. Biochemical testing confirmed catecholamine excess. He was started on oral doxazosin 1 mg daily, which was titrated to 2 mg daily after 1 week, followed by oral bisoprolol 2.5 mg daily in preparation for surgery. Five weeks later, he presented with severe right-sided abdominal pain and a blood pressure of 215/111 mmHg. Abdominal CT angiography showed interval enlargement of the adrenal mass with posterior rupture and a retroperitoneal hematoma without active bleeding. He was stabilized with conservative management and subsequently underwent robotic right adrenalectomy. Histopathology confirmed pheochromocytoma with necrosis, without angioinvasion or lymphatic invasion, and with negative margins. Pheochromocytoma rupture can occur despite appropriate α-blockade, and spontaneous hemorrhage remains the most likely proposed mechanism, although α-blockade may be a contributing factor in selected cases.

papers.title: Bone metastases identify a high-risk subgroup in metastatic neuroendocrine tumors with particular relevance in NETs of unknown primary.
papers.abstract: Bone metastases (BM) are an increasingly recognized manifestation of advanced neuroendocrine tumors (NETs), but their prevalence and association with survival in NETs of unknown primary (CUP NET) remain insufficiently characterized. We assessed the prevalence of BM and their association with overall survival (OS) in patients with metastatic pancreatic NETs (PanNETs), small intestinal NETs (siNETs), and CUP NETs. We conducted a retrospective analysis of 642 patients with histologically confirmed metastatic well-differentiated NETs who were treated at the European Neuroendocrine Tumour Society (ENETS) Center Essen between 2009 and 2023 using somatostatin-receptor (SSTR)- based hybrid imaging with 68Ga-DOTATOC PET/CT. The patients included 171 with PanNETs, 305 with siNETs, and 166 with CUP NETs. The primary outcome was OS, defined as the time from date of initial NET diagnosis to death from any cause. Secondary outcomes included BM prevalence, entity-specific survival according to BM status, BM morphology and timing, and skeletal-related events. BM were detected in 238 patients (37.1%) and were most frequent in CUP NETs (42.8%), followed by PanNETs (36.3%) and siNETs (34.4%). Median OS in the overall cohort was 77 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 64-89) in patients with BM and 141 months (95% CI, 119-186) in metastatic patients without BM (log-rank p < 0.001). In CUP NETs, median OS was 30 months in patients with BM and 66 months in metastatic patients without BM (log-rank p = 0.021). In multivariable Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, tumor grade, functioning status, and tumor entity, BM remained associated with shorter OS (hazard ratio [HR], 1.45; 95% CI, 1.13-1.85; p = 0.0034). In an entity-stratified model BM remained associated with OS (HR, 1.43; 95% CI, 1.09-1.89; p = 0.011). In the CUP NET subgroup, the adjusted HR associated with BM was 1.83 (95% CI, 1.17-2.85; p = 0.008). BM were common in patients with metastatic NETs and are particularly prevalent and clinically relevant in CUP NET.

papers.title: Editorial: Unveiling the complexity of neuroendocrine neoplasms: biomarkers, classification, and translational perspectives.
Adjuvant Immunotherapy for Resected Head and Neck Mucosal Melanoma: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Head and neck mucosal melanoma (HNMM) is a rare, aggressive malignancy with high recurrence rates and limited prospective data to guide postoperative management. While immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) have reshaped melanoma treatment, their survival impact in resected HNMM remains poorly defined. We evaluated real-world outcomes after curative-intent surgery and the association of adjuvant immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy with survival. We retrospectively identified patients with HNMM who underwent curative-intent surgery from 1990 to 2024. Overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) were estimated from surgery using Kaplan-Meier methods. Univariable Cox models evaluated associations of adjuvant ICI with survival. Among 89 patients, median follow-up was 38 months (IQR, 18-60). Most tumors arose in the nasal cavity or paranasal sinuses (72/89, 81%); 23 (26%) had T4 disease and 7 (8%) had regional nodal metastases. Among tested patients, BRAF, NRAS, and KIT alterations were identified in 4/37 (11%), 7/25 (28%), and 0/28 (0%), respectively. Median tumor mutational burden was 3.45 mutations/Mb (IQR, 2.15-7.95; n = 10) and median PD-L1 tumor proportion score was 0.5% (IQR, 0%-1%; n = 6). Seventeen patients (19%) received adjuvant ICI, including anti-PD-1 monotherapy (n = 10), CTLA-4 monotherapy (n = 1), or combination anti-PD-1/CTLA-4 therapy (n = 6); 48 (54%) received adjuvant radiotherapy. Two- and 5-year OS were 66% and 46%, respectively; corresponding PFS estimates were 65% and 46%. Adjuvant ICI was not associated with improved OS (hazard ratio [HR], 0.69; 95% CI, 0.31-1.55; p = 0.37) or PFS (HR, 1.06; 95% CI, 0.50-2.21; p = 0.88). Initial progression patterns were broadly similar between groups. In this single-institution cohort of surgically treated HNMM, adjuvant ICI was not associated with improved OS or PFS. Patterns of initial disease progression were similar between treatment groups, underscoring the need for more effective peri-operative strategies.

papers.title: Prognostic Comparison of Breast Neuroendocrine Neoplasms and Invasive Ductal Carcinoma With Neuroendocrine Differentiation: A Pathology-Reviewed Cohort and Population-Based Analysis.
papers.abstract: Breast neuroendocrine neoplasms (Br-NENs) are rare breast tumors with substantial clinicopathological heterogeneity. The prognostic implications of the 2019 World Health Organization (WHO) classification remain incompletely characterized. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic significance of true breast neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) and invasive ductal carcinoma with neuroendocrine differentiation (IDC-NE) under the 2019 WHO framework. We retrospectively analyzed a pathology-reviewed single-center cohort of 123 patients, of whom 121 were included in survival analyses, and a separate population-based cohort of 498 patients from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database. Institutional cases were reassessed according to the 2019 WHO criteria, whereas SEER tumor groups were defined using registry-reported International Classification of Diseases for Oncology, Third Edition (ICD-O-3) morphology codes. Survival outcomes were compared using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models. Sensitivity analyses were performed to assess robustness, while exploratory propensity score matching (PSM) analyses compared IDC-NE with conventional invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC). In the single-center cohort, true NENs showed more aggressive clinicopathological features and were associated with poorer survival than IDC-NE. In the SEER cohort, 498 patients were included, comprising 323 with registry-defined NEN and 175 with registry-defined IDC-NE. NEN showed more aggressive characteristics, including a higher rate of distant metastasis at diagnosis. After adjustment for age, stage, year of diagnosis, and race, registry-defined NEN was independently associated with worse overall survival (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.62, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.14-2.32) and breast cancer-specific survival (HR = 2.00, 95% CI 1.30-3.06). Sensitivity analyses yielded consistent results. Breast NENs were associated with poorer outcomes than IDC-NE in the pathology-reviewed cohort. The SEER analysis provided complementary population-based prognostic evidence for registry-defined tumor groups. Exploratory PSM analyses did not identify a statistically significant survival difference between IDC-NE and conventional IDC.

papers.title: Administrating Everolimus against neuroendocrine differentiated prostate cancer, a preliminary experience.
papers.abstract: Neuroendocrine prostate cancer (NEPC) is a deadly condition, with a median overall survival of less than one year after diagnosis. Although clinical trials are ongoing, an established treatment strategy for NEPC has not yet been developed. A recent clinical trial, RADIANT-4, showed that treatment with everolimus significantly improved survival in patients with progressive neuroendocrine tumors of the lung or gastrointestinal tract. This study evaluated the efficacy of everolimus against neuroendocrine differentiated prostate cancer as an initial investigation. Five patients with neuroendocrine differentiated prostate cancer were treated with everolimus (10 mg daily). In our study, we examined the responses and changes over time of circulating neuroendocrine tumor markers, including neuron-specific enolase (NSE) and pro-gastrin-releasing peptide (pro-GRP). We also evaluated survival outcomes such as castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC)-free survival, overall survival (OS), and cancer-specific survival (CSS). The median follow-up duration was 32 months. A decline in circulating neuroendocrine tumor markers was observed in all cases. The median decline rate of NSE was -0.417, and that of pro-GRP was -0.647 (p = 0.841). The median CRPC-free survival was 10 months (range: 3-NA). Median CSS and OS were both 32 months (range: 8-NA). Grade 3 adverse events (AEs) included hyperglycemia and pneumonitis. Grade 1 AEs included stomatitis (2 cases), paronychia, and pneumonitis. Everolimus demonstrated reductions in circulating neuroendocrine markers in this exploratory cohort of prostate adenocarcinoma with neuroendocrine differentiation; however, these findings are descriptive and do not establish treatment efficacy.

papers.title: Patients with neuroendocrine neoplasms referred to the palliative care teams of tertiary care centers: a multicenter retrospective descriptive study.
papers.abstract: Neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) can be divided into well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors and poorly differentiated carcinomas (NETs and NECs, respectively). Although the incidence of NENs is increasing globally, reports on palliative care in affected populations are scarce. This study aimed to describe the state of palliative care team (PCT) interventions for patients with NENs referred to tertiary care centers' PCTs. Among the patients with neoplasms referred to tertiary care centers' PCTs during January 2017-June 2025, those histopathologically diagnosed with NENs were included. They were classified as having NETs or NECs, and baseline characteristics, reason for PCT referral, and outcomes after PCT intervention were investigated. Additionally, for patients referred to a PCT because of pain, the numerical rating scale (NRS) score, cause of pain, pain type, pain management details, and the equivalent oral morphine dose (EOMD) were also investigated. These parameters were compared between patients with NETs and NECs. Among 3,190 patients with neoplasms referred to tertiary care centers' PCTs, 48 (1.5%) had NENs, including 32 with NETs and 16 with NECs. Pain was the most common reason for PCT consultation (39/48 patients). Patients with NECs had significantly higher NRS scores and EOMD at consultation and a significantly higher mortality. Non-neoplastic pain was also identified in 5 patients (12.8%), for whom PCT-led opioid tapering and discontinuation were promoted to ensure appropriate opioid use. Given the diverse clinical course of NENs, research on palliative care and pain control for affected patients must be further deepened.

papers.title: Stage-Associated Collagen Gene Expression and Macrophage-Associated Immune Features in Nail Unit Melanoma.
papers.abstract: Acral melanoma, a rare subtype arising on the palms, soles, and nail unit, responds poorly to immune checkpoint inhibitors. Among acral melanomas, nail unit melanoma is less common than plantar melanoma, and the transcriptomic programs associated with its progression remain poorly understood. We performed bulk RNA sequencing of 43 nail unit melanoma specimens from early- to late-stage disease. Unsupervised clustering identified two transcriptomic groups that were associated with clinical stage, with one group enriched for late-stage tumors and the other for early-stage tumors. The late-stage-enriched group showed higher expression of collagen/extracellular matrix (ECM) genes involved in collagen processing, assembly, and remodeling, whereas the early-stage-enriched group showed higher expression of epidermal and basement membrane-associated genes. In the late-stage-enriched group, deconvolution showed higher macrophage and lower CD8+ T cell estimates, and SPP1 and APOE were more highly expressed; both genes also showed higher expression in late-stage tumors. Across tumors, macrophage and tumor-associated macrophage signature scores correlated positively with a collagen biosynthesis gene-set score, including after adjustment for histological tumor purity. Several stage-associated differences were attenuated after purity adjustment. These tissue-level associations describe collagen/ECM- and macrophage-associated features of nail unit melanoma; their cellular origin and clinical relevance require independent evaluation.

papers.title: Hybrid Imaging in the Head and Neck: Focus on Somatostatin Receptor Imaging-DOTATATE is Great!
papers.abstract: In head and neck imaging somatostatin receptor (SSTR) imaging with DOTATATE has markedly improved detection of meningiomas compared to schwannomas as well as preoperative surgical or radiation therapy planning and posttreatment surveillance. DOTATATE is great for detection of paragangliomas, pituitary tumors, olfactory neuroblastoma, neuroendocrine neoplasms and medullary thyroid cancer. DOTATATE is useful in identifying multiple paragangliomas especially if hereditary, multiple endocrine tumors in genetic syndromes and medullary thyroid cancer and may potentially assessment of middle ear adenomas, pituitary neuroendocrine tumors and olfactory neuroblastoma. SSTR PET may help predict response to targeted tumor treatment with peptide receptor radionuclide therapy.

papers.title: Surgical Approaches and Extent of Resection for Non-myasthenic Thymic Epithelial Tumors:Current Evidence and Future Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Thymic epithelial tumors are rare anterior mediastinal neoplasms that include thymoma, thymic carcinoma, and neuroendocrine tumors. Complete surgical resection remains the cornerstone of curative treatment;however, the optimal extent of thymectomy and surgical approach are still being debated. Advances in minimally invasive techniques, such as video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery and robot-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (RATS), have shifted practice away from traditional median sternotomy. Evidence consistently shows that complete resection is the most important prognostic factor across all subtypes. Regarding early-stage thymoma, multicenter and propensity score-matched studies showed that partial thymectomy may achieve similar oncologic outcomes to total thymectomy, with shorter hospital stays and reduced perioperative morbidity. Conversely, total thymectomy remains essential for thymic carcinoma or invasive disease. Minimally invasive approaches, particularly RATS, offer advantages including precise dissection in narrow mediastinal spaces, less blood loss, and faster recovery without compromising the margin status or long-term survival. Emerging data also suggest potential long-term immunological and oncologic consequences of total thymectomy in adults, underscoring the need for individualized surgical planning. Overall, current evidence supports tailoring the extent and approach of thymectomy according to the histological subtype, tumor stage, and patient factors, balancing oncologic radicality with the preservation of physiological thymic function. papers.title: Imaging characteristics of orbital involvement in patients with neuroendocrine neoplasms: a report of two cases.
papers.abstract: This case series presents clinical and radiological findings of two patients with orbital involvement of neuroendocrine neoplasm (NEN) and discusses imaging characteristics in the context of modern literature.Full ophthalmic examination and orthoptic assessment were completed in two patients. Magnetic resonance imaging of the orbit and brain was carried out using 1.5 Tesla MRI (Siemens Symphony, Erlangen, Germany)Despite different systemic involvement (Patient 1: primary lesion in the caecum, with multiple deposits in the liver, left iliac crest, myocardium, pleura, paratracheal region and paraoesophageal nodes; patient 2: skin and pituitary lesions) in all patients in this case series, orbital MRI showed a lobulated, well-circumscribed lesion adherent or involving extraocular muscles. In both cases, orbital involvement was not isolated. Brain and scalp lesions in patient 2 had similar lobulated heterogeneous appearance.This case series highlights the importance of systemic work-up of patients presenting with NEN to assess for both primary and extent of disease. Multi-disciplinary team involvement is essential to provide patients with a correct diagnosis and appropriate management promptly.

papers.title: PD-L1 testing in cutaneous malignancies: interpretation, clinical utility, and unresolved challenges.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors have transformed the management of melanoma, cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC), Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC), basal cell carcinoma (BCC), and selected rare cutaneous malignancies, yet the clinical value of programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) immunohistochemistry has not kept pace with the therapeutic importance of the PD-1/PD-L1 pathway. This narrative review, prepared according to the SANRA quality criteria, evaluates PD-L1 testing at four linked levels: what PD-L1 expression represents biologically, how reliably it can be measured, whether it is prognostic or predictive, and whether the result changes clinical management. PD-L1 expression is inducible, spatially and temporally heterogeneous, and present on tumor and immune cells, and its measurement depends on specimen, clone, platform, scored compartment, and cutoff. In melanoma, tumor-cell PD-L1 enriches for response at the cohort level, but PD-L1-negative tumors respond to PD-1 blockade, and the only label that mandates testing is the European authorization of nivolumab-relatlimab for tumor-cell PD-L1 < 1%. In cSCC, MCC, and BCC, checkpoint inhibitors are approved without PD-L1 selection, and no PD-L1 companion diagnostic is approved for any cutaneous malignancy. PD-L1 should therefore be reported with the specimen, clone, platform, compartment, scoring system, and cutoff, and interpreted only within a defined tumor and therapeutic context. Composite approaches that integrate tumor immunogenicity, CD8-positive T cell spatial organization, interferon-gamma signaling, viral status, circulating tumor DNA, and multiplex or digital pathology are more likely than PD-L1 alone to improve treatment selection, but they must demonstrate incremental, reproducible clinical utility.

papers.title: Validation of the International Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma Grading System in a Multicenter Cohort: Digital Image Analysis-Based Evaluation of Ki-67 Cutoffs and Assessment Methods.
papers.abstract: Although the International Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma Grading System (IMTCGS) was proposed to standardize the histologic grading of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), the validity of its 5% Ki-67 index cutoff and the optimal assessment method remain to be fully established. This multicenter study aimed to validate the Ki-67 index component of the IMTCGS in a Korean cohort using digital image analysis (DIA) and to determine the most clinically relevant evaluation method. We retrospectively analyzed 187 surgically resected MTC cases across 16 institutions. Ki-67 indices were evaluated via DIA using two approaches: the hotspot method (highest proliferative area) and the average method (across three representative regions). Prognostic values of various Ki-67 cutoffs (5%, 3%, and ROC curve-derived thresholds) were evaluated independently and within the IMTCGS framework. IMTCGS high-grade status incorporating the 5% hotspot Ki-67 index emerged as an independent prognostic factor for recurrence-free survival (RFS), along with male sex, elevated postoperative serum calcitonin levels, and pN1b status. IMTCGS grading using the 5% average Ki-67 index failed to retain independent significance. While the composite high-grade IMTCGS classification remained an independent predictor of RFS in multivariate analysis, none of its constituent components (tumor necrosis, mitotic count, or Ki-67 index) retained independent prognostic significance when evaluated separately. This multicenter study validates the prognostic utility of the IMTCGS in Korean MTC patients. DIA-based hotspot Ki-67 assessment provides superior prognostic stratification compared to the average method, supporting its preference for routine clinical IMTCGS implementation.

papers.title: Risk factor analysis of nodal and distant metastasis for G1 and G2 gastric neuroendocrine tumors.
papers.abstract: Gastric neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) are a group of rare diseases, and we aimed to describe their clinicopathological features and explore the risk factors affecting metastatic disease. A retrospective analysis of 1480 patients with gastric NETs who underwent surgical resection from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results database between 2010 and 2019 was performed. Logistic regression analyses were conducted to identify the independent risk factors for regional lymph node metastasis and distant metastasis. The Kaplan‒Meier method was used to calculate cancer-specific survival rates. Cumulative incidence of cancer-specific mortality was calculated by a competing risk model. Of the 1480 patients, 1142 (77.2%) had G1 NETs, and 338 (22.8%) had G2 NETs. With regard to tumor size, 950 (64.2%) had primary neoplasms smaller than 1 cm, 302 (20.4%) had neoplasms within 1 to 2 cm in size, and 228 (15.4%) had neoplasms larger than or equal to 2 cm. Lymph node and distant metastases were identified through a comprehensive evaluation of imaging examinations. In total, 90 (6.1%) and 40 (2.7%) patients had regional lymph node metastasis and distant metastasis, respectively. Logistic regression analysis revealed that sex (P = .011), race (P = .049), tumor size (P < .001), and T stage (P < 001) were the independent risk factors for regional lymph node metastasis, while tumor grade (P = .033) and regional lymph node metastasis (P < .001) were the independent risk factors for distant metastasis. Survival analysis demonstrated that patients with gastric NETs had a favorable prognosis, with 3-year, 5-year, and 10-year cancer-specific survival rates of 97.4%, 96.1%, and 94.5%, respectively. Gastric NETs are generally slow-growing with favorable outcomes, though metastasis is possible. Tumor size and T stage primarily influence regional lymph node metastasis, whereas tumor grade and regional lymph node involvement are key risks for distant metastasis.

papers.title: A case of pituitary neuroendocrine carcinoma defying survival timeline.
papers.abstract: Metastatic pituitary neuroendocrine tumours (PitNETs) are exceedingly rare, accounting for less than 0.2% of all pituitary tumours; they typically have a poor prognosis, with patient survival limited to 2-4 years because of aggressive local invasion and metastatic spread. We describe a unique case of a 50-year-old man with an adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)-secreting pituitary macroadenoma initially resected in 2007 who subsequently developed multiple recurrences and ultimately developed a metastatic PitNET. The patient underwent repeated surgical resections, stereotactic radiosurgery, radiotherapy, and systemic therapies, including temozolomide (TMZ), peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT), and somatostatin analogues. Histopathology evolved from a low-grade to high-grade PitNET with a Ki-67 index of up to 50%, although p53 remained negative, possibly contributing to his unusually prolonged survival. Notably, methylation of the O-6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase (MGMT) promoter likely enhanced the patient's favourable response to TMZ. Despite multiple intracranial and extracranial metastases, including involvement of the temporal lobe, parotid gland, and scapular bone, the patient survived for 17 years from the initial diagnosis and for 9 years from a confirmed metastatic disease, defying the typical prognosis. This case highlights the importance of vigilant long-term surveillance; the recognition of prognostic markers, such as Ki-67, p53, and MGMT status; and the role of multimodal therapy, including surgery, radiotherapy, and TMZ, in extending survival in patients with aggressive pituitary tumours. Although metastatic PitNETs generally portend a dismal outcome, individualised and sequential treatment strategies can occasionally result in exceptional long-term survival.

papers.title: Controversies in NEN: An ENETS position statement on unresolved clinical scenarios and emerging approaches with somatostatin analogues.
papers.abstract: Somatostatin analogues (SSAs) are the cornerstone of treatment for patients with neuroendocrine tumours (NETs), with established anti-secretory activity in functioning NETs and anti-proliferative activity in grade 1 and 2 (Ki-67 levels, up to 10%) gastro-entero-pancreatic NETs. However, several clinically relevant scenarios regarding their role still remain insufficiently addressed by available guidance, including the following: patient selection for dose-escalation or interval-shortening after disease progression, their anti-proliferative effect in tumours with a > 10% Ki-67 index, their role in pulmonary carcinoids, Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia (MEN1)-related pancreatic NETs and uncommon neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs), their adjuvant use after surgery, and their continuation beyond disease progression, as well as the presence of predictive biomarkers, quality-of-life endpoints, and emerging somatostatin receptor (SSTR)-targeted strategies. This manuscript addresses 10 practical questions regarding SSA use beyond established indications. The available evidence supports dose-intensification mainly for improved hormonal symptom control and, in selected patients, temporary disease stabilisation, while objective tumour responses remain uncommon. Anti-proliferative effects may also be observed in some grade 2 NETs with a Ki-67 index higher than 10%, albeit with diminishing activity in the presence of increasing proliferative activity, whereas it is limited in grade 3 tumours. Evidence in pulmonary carcinoids, MEN1-related pancreatic NETs, and other uncommon somatostatin receptor (SSTR)-positive NETs remains heterogeneous, and mostly based on small or non-randomised studies. In contrast, routine adjuvant treatment after complete tumour resection is not currently supported, although retrospective studies suggest a potential benefit in selected patients with resected pancreatic NETs at high risk of recurrence. Quantitative SSTR imaging, tissue SSTR2 expression and circulating molecular markers are promising tools for patient selection, but none is currently validated for routine predictive use. New formulations and SSTR-directed agents with receptor-binding properties distinct from those of conventional SSAs are expected to broaden future treatment options, although their clinical value will require prospective confirmation.

papers.title: Ectopic ACTH Syndrome Presenting as Refractory Hypokalemia in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer with Neuroendocrine Transformation.
papers.abstract: Ectopic adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) syndrome resulting from neuroendocrine transformation of prostate adenocarcinoma may present with refractory hypokalemia as an initial manifestation. Because hypokalemia is often attributed to other more common aetiologies, the diagnosis is often overlooked, leading to delayed management. A 62-year-old man with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) with neuroendocrine transformation presented with persistent hypokalemia. He later developed severe hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis, and hypertension with disease progression. Endocrine workup revealed markedly elevated cortisol, no suppression on low dose dexamethasone testing, and elevated ACTH. Imaging showed no pituitary or adrenal lesions but demonstrated progression of metastatic disease. These findings supported ectopic ACTH secretion secondary to neuroendocrine transformation. Before initiation of the appropriate treatment, he developed supraventricular tachycardia, hypotension, pulmonary edema, and died. This case underscores the importance of considering paraneoplastic endocrine syndromes, such as ectopic ACTH secretion, in patients with malignancies and unexplained or refractory electrolyte disturbances-particularly in the context of neuroendocrine transformation. Neuroendocrine transformation of prostate cancer is a rare but clinically significant cause of ectopic adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) syndrome.A high index of suspicion for ectopic ACTH syndrome is warranted in patients with prostate cancer with unexplained or refractory hypokalemia, especially in known or suspected neuroendocrine transformation.

papers.title: From histopathology to molecular taxonomy: predicting pituitary neuroendocrine tumors invasiveness.
papers.abstract: Pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs) are among the most prevalent intracranial tumors in adults. Although most follow an indolent clinical course, a substantial subset exhibits local invasion, which can limit gross total resection and increase the risk of residual disease and recurrence. Importantly, anatomical invasiveness should not be equated with clinical aggressiveness. Aggressive PitNETs may also exhibit a longitudinal pattern of repeated or multiple local recurrences and frequently require multiple therapeutic interventions. The 2022 Fifth Edition of the WHO Classification formally renamed pituitary adenomas to PitNETs and established a lineage classification framework centered on core transcription factors, including PIT1, TPIT, and SF1, thereby driving the transition from traditional pathological diagnosis to molecular subtyping. Driven by recent advances in high-throughput sequencing, liquid biopsy, and single-cell omics, numerous novel molecular biomarkers have emerged, enabling the early pre- and postoperative identification of invasive subpopulations. This review systematically outlines recent progress in multidimensional biomarkers-including DNA methylation, protein markers, non-coding RNAs, liquid biopsy indicators, and tumor microenvironmental features-to provide an updated synthesis of candidate biomarkers that may support future risk stratification and individualized management of invasive PitNETs.

papers.title: [Comparison of clinical characteristics and MRI functional parameters between choroidal melanoma and choroidal hemangioma].
papers.abstract: Objective: To investigate the potential value of clinical characteristics and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) functional parameters in the auxiliary differential diagnosis of choroidal melanoma and choroidal hemangioma. Methods: This retrospective case series included patients who underwent orbital MRI at the Department of Ophthalmology, Shanghai Ninth People's Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine between September 2023 and December 2025 and were clinically or pathologically diagnosed with choroidal melanoma (choroidal melanoma group) or choroidal hemangioma (choroidal hemangioma group). Demographic characteristics, tumor morphologic parameters (largest basal diameter and tumor thickness), semiquantitative dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI parameters, and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) values were compared between the two groups. The receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed for parameters that remained statistically significant after false discovery rate correction using the Benjamini-Hochberg method. Results: A total of 30 patients (30 eyes) with choroidal melanoma and 12 patients (12 eyes) with choroidal hemangioma were included. There were no statistically significant differences in age, sex, or laterality of the affected eye between the two groups (all P>0.05). The largest basal diameter [11.02 (3.18, 17.37) mm] and tumor thickness [8.04 (3.10, 12.93) mm] were greater in the choroidal melanoma group than in the choroidal hemangioma group [7.83 (6.30, 11.03) mm and 3.06 (1.35, 4.28) mm, respectively] (all adjusted P<0.001). The relative peak intensity [1.32 (1.08, 2.91)], maximum enhancement [203.81 (28.40, 763.83)], maximum relative enhancement percentage [25.95% (4.90%, 194.09%)], wash-in rate [17.19 (0, 53.13)/s], area under the time-signal intensity curve [9 920.43 (383.03, 50 447.50)], and ADC [0.85×10-³ (0.63×10-³, 1.51×10-³) mm²/s] were all lower in the choroidal melanoma group than in the choroidal hemangioma group (all adjusted P<0.001). The initial time was higher in the choroidal melanoma group [36.48 (4.47, 95.22) s] than in the choroidal hemangioma group [25.18 (16.90, 27.96) s] (adjusted P<0.05). No statistically significant differences were observed between the two groups in outflow percentage, time to peak, wash-out rate, brevity of enhancement, or TTP-T0 (all adjusted P>0.05). The distribution of time-signal intensity curve types also did not differ significantly between groups (P>0.05). Several parameters showed relatively high areas under the ROC curve; the area under the ROC curve was 1.000 for ADC (95% confidence interval: 1.000 to 1.000) and 0.981 for maximum relative enhancement percentage (95% confidence interval: 0.933 to 1.000). Conclusions: Choroidal melanoma and choroidal hemangioma showed marked differences in tumor size and multiple MRI functional parameters. The maximum relative enhancement percentage among the semiquantitative dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI parameters and ADC showed relatively high exploratory discriminatory performance and may provide complementary quantitative information for the differential diagnosis of these two diseases.
