papers.title: A rare case of endobronchial carcinoid causing recurrent pneumothorax: a case report.
papers.abstract: Endobronchial carcinoid tumor rarely causes secondary spontaneous pneumothorax. We report a female in her 30s who reported progressive decline in her overall exercise tolerance with dyspnea on exertion and frequent upper respiratory infections (URIs) for 2 years presented for persistent spontaneous pneumothorax (SP). Initially, she presented to the emergency department (ED) for concerns of cough with mild hemoptysis and congestion for 2 weeks. She was found to have a small left-sided pneumothorax. She was admitted and treated for community-acquired pneumonia (CAP). Post-hospital follow-up showed a persistent pneumothorax unchanged in size. She was followed for weeks with serial chest X-rays, which later showed an increased size of the pneumothorax. She was admitted, and a chest tube was placed. Later, bronchoscopy was done, which showed near complete occlusion of the left mainstem bronchus by an endobronchial lesion. Pathology results showed a well-differentiated neuroendocrine grade 1 tumor consistent with carcinoid. She was successfully treated with tumor resection and photodynamic therapy (PDT). This case highlighted an unusual presentation of an endobronchial carcinoid tumor that requires further diagnostic workup with appropriate intervention.

papers.title: Galangin Exerts Neuroprotective Effects in Spinal Cord Injury by Targeting the PI3K/AKT and JAK2/STAT1 Pathways.
papers.abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) often leads to permanent neurological deficits, with no effective treatment currently available. Galangin is a naturally occurring flavonoid with anti-inflammatory and antiapoptotic activities; nevertheless, its efficacy, and molecular mechanisms in SCI remain unelucidated. First, network pharmacology and Gene Expression Omnibus database analyses were used to predict target molecules and galangin signaling pathways. In vitro, LPS-induced immortalized murine microglial (BV-2) and rat pheochromocytoma (PC12) cells co-cultured with conditioned medium were used to elucidate the mechanism via western blotting, immunofluorescence, qRT-PCR, ELISA, flow cytometry, cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA), drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS), surface plasmon resonance (SPR), and pathway agonist/inhibitor/siRNA rescue assays. In vivo, SCI rat models were established to validate the protective efficacy through behavioral, histological, and western blot analyses. Galangin alleviated pro-inflammatory polarization and neuroinflammation in BV-2 microglia through inhibiting the PI3K/AKT pathway. It also diminished neuronal apoptosis and enhanced axonal growth-associated markers expression in PC12 neurons by inhibiting the JAK2/STAT1 pathway. These mechanisms were further supported experimentally using pathway agonists, inhibitors, and gene knockdown. In rats, galangin improved motor function and reduced neuroinflammation and neuronal damage. In conclusion, galangin simultaneously inhibited both pathways to alleviate neuroinflammation, decrease neuronal damage, and upregulate axonal growth-associated markers, thereby improving neurological function in SCI. Thus, galangin is a potential protective candidate for SCI.

papers.title: Temporal dynamics and prognostic value of serum calcitonin during tirzepatide therapy in adults with obesity.
papers.abstract: To characterize serum calcitonin dynamics during six months of tirzepatide therapy for obesity and explore whether early changes are associated with subsequent biochemical behavior. This prospective observational study enrolled 77 adults with obesity initiating tirzepatide. One participant diagnosed with medullary thyroid carcinoma at baseline was excluded, leaving 76 participants for longitudinal analysis. Serum calcitonin was assessed at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months. Longitudinal changes were evaluated using non-parametric tests and mixed-effects models; prognostic analyses were exploratory. Median calcitonin increased modestly from 2.05 pg/mL at baseline to 2.12 pg/mL at 3 months and 2.25 pg/mL at 6 months, with a significant overall time effect (p < 0.001) but no further significant change between 3 and 6 months (p = 0.43). Two participants with baseline calcitonin < 12 pg/mL developed new-onset elevations ≥ 12 pg/mL during early follow-up; no additional cases occurred at 6 months. Early calcitonin change was strongly associated with six-month change (Spearman ρ=0.73, p < 0.001), although prognostic analyses were limited by only two threshold events. Median weight loss was 8.3% and 15.0% at 3 and 6 months, respectively. Tirzepatide was associated with a small early increase in serum calcitonin followed by stabilization through six months. Early calcitonin changes were associated with subsequent biochemical behavior, but the limited follow-up and small number of threshold events preclude conclusions regarding prognostic cutoffs or monitoring strategies.

papers.title: Early-onset Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumors: Distinct and Age-Related Metabolic Profiles.
papers.abstract: Early-onset pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (EO-PanNETs) exhibit distinct clinical features, but their metabolic profiles and age-related associations remain poorly understood. This study included 641 patients with PanNETs from four tertiary centers in China. EO-PanNETs were defined as PanNETs diagnosed before 50 years. 1,282 hospital-based nonmalignant controls were matched 1:2 by age and sex. Conditional logistic regression and Cox models were used to assess associations with PanNET occurrence and survival outcomes, respectively. Age-related effect modification was assessed using exposure-by-age interaction terms, with age modeled continuously using restricted cubic splines (RCS) in sensitivity analyses. Compared with late-onset cases, EO-PanNETs exhibited a higher prevalence of reduced high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (29.2% vs 17.8%, P < 0.001). Although the overall prevalence of diabetes was similar between EO-PanNETs and LO-PanNETs, the proportion of new-onset cases among patients with diabetes was higher in EO-PanNETs(71.4% vs. 44.8%, P = 0.018). In case-control analyses using matched nonmalignant controls as reference, alcohol intake (OR, 1.77 vs. 0.79; P interaction = 0.008), diabetes mellitus (OR, 9.72 vs. 3.34; P interaction = 0.048) and elevated triglycerides (OR, 1.75 vs. 1.01; P interaction = 0.023) showed stronger associations with PanNET occurrence in younger individuals. EO-PanNETs also exhibited better overall survival and progression-free survival than LO-PanNETs. RCS analyses further identified age-related differences in the associations of alcohol intake and overweight with PanNET occurrence. These findings highlight age-related differences in the associations of metabolic factors with PanNETs, providing new insights into age-related metabolic heterogeneity in this rare disease.

papers.title: A Proposal for a PitNET Staging System: A Springboard for International Discussion.
Gq-coupled GPCRs mediate the oncogenic activity of Gαq-Q209L/P mutants in uveal melanoma cells.
papers.abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) stimulate heterotrimeric G proteins (Gαβγ) to facilitate downstream signaling, termination of which relies on a glutamine (Q) residue at position 209 in G protein α subunits. In uveal melanoma (UM), the most common intraocular malignancy in adults, >90% of patients harbor Q209L (QL) or Q209P (QP) mutations in Gαq and Gα11 proteins. Although mutationally active Gα subunits are thought to signal independently of GPCRs, some constitutively active Gα subunits may retain the ability to bind to GPCRs. Here, we demonstrated that Gq-coupled GPCRs, including 5-hydroxytryptamine receptor 2B (HTR2B), enhanced the oncogenic signaling of Gαq-QL. Although HTR2B antagonists alone had little to no inhibitory effects, they enhanced the sensitivity of UM cells to the Gαq-specific inhibitor YM-254890, as measured by signaling, cell viability, and proliferation assays. Last, treatment of UM cells with HTR2B antagonists and low concentrations of YM-254890 shifted endogenous Gαq-QL/QP mutants into an inactive conformation to a greater extent than did YM-254890 alone. Our study demonstrates that Gq-coupled GPCRs enhance the oncogenicity of mutationally active Gαq proteins and that antagonism of HTR2B promotes an inactive state of Gαq-QL/QP that increases sensitivity to an inhibitor of Gαq.

papers.title: Сomparative analysis of machine learning models for survival prediction in patients with malignant melanoma.
papers.abstract: Aim: To perform a comparative analysis of the effectiveness of contemporary machine learning models applied to survival prediction in patients with malignant melanoma and to assess their potential advantages over conventional staging systems as tools for personalised risk stratification. Materials and Methods: A structured comparative analysis of published prognostic models developed using population-based databases was performed, comparing measures of discrimination (area under the ROC curve [AUC] and concordance index [C-index]), calibration (Brier score), and clinical utility (decision curve analysis). The clinical context was supplemented by data from a retrospective cohort study of patients with cutaneous melanoma. Results: Ensemble and gradient-boosting algorithms (Random Forest, CatBoost, and XGBoost) consistently outperformed Cox proportional hazards regression models in terms of discrimination, achieving AUC values of approximately 0.76-0.84 for 1-, 3-, and 5-year survival. Ensemble models achieved a C-index of 0.732, compared with 0.685 for Cox regression and 0.537 for AJCC/NCCN criteria; the MIA nomogram demonstrated performance comparable to that of machine learning models (C-index, 0.739). Tumour stage, age, and surgical treatment were consistently identified as the leading prognostic factors. Retrospective cohort data confirmed the prognostic role of Breslow thickness, mitotic activity, and lymph node involvement in disease progression. Conclusions: Machine learning models provide greater accuracy and more individualised prognostic assessment than conventional approaches and may serve as a supplement to standard staging systems. Their implementation requires prospective validation while preserving the physician's ultimate decision-making authority.

papers.title: MCAM is Expressed in a Subset of Advanced Cutaneous Melanomas.
papers.abstract: Melanoma Cell Adhesion Molecule (MCAM) is an attractive therapeutic target for several cutting-edge treatment modalities currently in development. To better understand patient subsets with the potential to benefit from MCAM targeting, MCAM protein levels were evaluated in 451 primary and metastatic cutaneous melanoma specimens. Expression was observed in the tumor cells of 35% of specimens and was associated with metastasis and with survival in metastatic cutaneous melanoma.

papers.title: Human Urine-Derived Induced Pluripotent Stem Cell Membranes Enable Personalized Transdermal Nanotherapy for Melanoma.
papers.abstract: Melanoma treatment remains limited by drug resistance, immune-related adverse effects, and inadequate tumor-specific drug delivery. Nanoparticle (NP)-based delivery platforms have shown promise, but their clinical translation is hindered by rapid immune clearance and suboptimal biocompatibility. Current membrane-coating strategies often depend on invasive cell sources and lack patient-specific applicability. This study introduces a personalized melanoma therapy platform that integrates MnO2 NPs (MNPs) coated with urine-derived induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) membranes into a hydrogel-based transdermal patch. The patient-derived iPSC membrane enhances tumor targeting and immune evasion through the CXCR4/CXCL12 axis, while the MNPs facilitate pH-responsive release of cytotoxic drugs within the tumor microenvironment, maximizing therapeutic efficacy. The hydrogel transdermal patch enables direct, noninvasive delivery to skin lesions, promoting sustained drug exposure and potentially improving patient compliance. By combining autologous cell membrane coating, pH-responsive nanocarriers, and transdermal administration, this platform addresses key limitations of current melanoma therapies and supports the potential for clinical translation of personalized nanomedicine.

papers.title: Hematologic changes under [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE PRRT in GEP-NETs: a long-term longitudinal cohort study.
papers.abstract: Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) with [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE is increasingly applied for advanced gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (GEP-NETs). This study aimed to characterize the development of hematologic parameters under PRRT in a large single-center cohort. We retrospectively analyzed 178 patients with GEP-NETs treated with [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE at a university hospital (2012-2023). Hemoglobin (Hb), white blood cell count (WBC), and platelet count (PLT) were assessed at baseline, after 2 cycles (FU1), after 4 cycles (FU2), during post-therapy follow-up (FU3), and at the last available timepoint (FU4). Patients with deteriorating blood values during or after therapy were categorized according to CTCAE v6.0. The occurrence of myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) within the period from completion of the initial PRRT to initiation of salvage chemotherapy or PRRT was investigated. Baseline mean values were Hb, 13.6 ± 1.6 g/dL; WBC, 6.9 ± 2.0 × 10⁹/L; and PLT, 256 ± 92 × 10⁹/L. A significant decline in those hematological parameters was observed at FU1 and FU2 (p < 0.01). Between FU2 and FU3, values recovered significantly (p < 0.001), with no further relevant change at FU4 for Hb and PLT, while WBC increased significantly compared to FU3. At last follow-up (FU4), all parameters remained significantly below baseline (all p < 0.001), but exhibited final values in a normal laboratory range (Hb, 12.4 ± 1.9 g/dL; WBC, 6.3 ± 2.6 × 10⁹/L; and PLT, 216 ± 78 × 10⁹/L). Based on CTCAE v6.0, only 4 patients (2%) developed grade 3 hematological adverse events and no grade 4 adverse event was observed. After completing four cycles of PRRT, 2 patients (1.3%) developed MDS according to the WHO criteria. Patients with chemotherapy prior to PRRT (n = 30) had lower baseline WBC and showed smaller on-treatment declines, but were the only subgroup without Hb recovery from the nadir (median change FU2 to FU4, - 0.35 vs. +0.35 g/dL; adjusted p = 0.017). PRRT with [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE induces a mild short to midterm decline in hematologic parameters, which is followed by a significant increase during long-term follow-up, eventually returning to values within the laboratory reference range. Serious adverse events or MDS are very rare, supporting long-term overall hematologic safety.

papers.title: Bulk Transcriptomic Inference in Vestibular Schwannoma is Sensitive to Estimated Cell Composition: Cross-Cohort Analysis and Single-Cell Lineage Annotation.
papers.abstract: Bulk transcriptomic differences between vestibular schwannoma (VS) and nerve reflect both gene-expression differences and tissue composition. We evaluated composition sensitivity in GSE39645 (31 VS; nine nerve/Schwann-cell controls), compared a fixed 346-gene set with GSE108524 (27 VS, including 10 sporadic and 17 NF2-related cases; four nerve controls), and used GSE230375 for deconvolution and donor-level pseudobulk. Tumor-only GSE216783 supplied a second reference, while GSE250061 supported descriptive broad-lineage annotation. In the prespecified group-plus-batch model with five MuSiC composition principal components, 326 of 1,410 baseline differentially expressed genes retained both false-discovery rate < 0.05 and absolute log2 fold change > 1 thresholds; 1,084 lost at least one threshold, including 117 with reversed direction, and 405 were adjusted-only threshold calls. The primary design had group variance-inflation factor (VIF) 8.747; 303/500 sample-stratified bootstrap draws exceeded VIF 10 but remained full rank and were retained. Across the fixed 346 genes, direction concordance was 93.4% for all VS, 94.5% for sporadic cases and 93.6% for NF2-related cases. All-VS Pearson correlation was 0.883 (95% percentile interval 0.834-0.897); intervals were conditional on fixed references, annotations and gene set. A 20 + 20 + 20-repeat simulation showed fewer conditional beta-zero composition-only calls but greater expression-only standard errors and root-mean-square coefficient error, with VIF > 10 in 4/20 estimated-MuSiC and 3/20 oracle strong-scenario fits; all fits remained full rank. These analyses quantify model sensitivity; neither broad-lineage assignment nor simulation establishes mechanism, biomarkers or therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Explainable machine learning predictive models for treatment response after SBRT in melanoma brain metastases.
papers.abstract: To develop an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) model to predict the complete/partial response of oligometastatic brain lesions from melanoma (MBMs) two months after from radiosurgical or fractionated stereotactic treatments. 50 consecutive patients with a total 102 MBMs treated with CyberKnife® SBRT from December 2012 to December 2018 were selected within the Rabbit study. Local response was evaluated on brain MRI performed during follow-up using response evaluation criteria in solid tumors (RECIST) and revised using response criteria for brain metastases from the response assessment in neuro-oncology criteria (RANO) group. For each treated lesion, the following variables were considered: number of treated lesions, the LDH pre-treatment level, previous treatments (surgery or whole brain RT), BRAF status, time from primary diagnosis to brain lesions discovery (Time_diag), lesion dimensions and site, SBRT dose and fractionation, type of concomitant treatment with ipilimumab (IPI). Six different supervised machine learning models, including logistic regression (LR), k-nearest neighbors (KNN), support vector machine (SVM), random forest (RF), decision tree (DT) and light gradient boosting (LGBM), were trained and internally validated with 5-fold cross validation. Model performances were assessed using receiving operator curves (ROC) and area under the curve (AUC). An explainable approach based on SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method was deployed to generate individual explanations of the model decisions. Lastly, a decision tree was created to better understand and interpret the complex relationships between the covariates and the target variable. 23.5% of lesions had a complete or partial response and were used as ground truth for the ML models. The best performing model was the LGBM, reporting a mean AUCs in the 5-fold cross validation of 0.87 (0.85-0.91). SHAP analysis strongly associated complete/partial response with four variables, namely in order of importance: the BRAF status, the total dose, the type of treatment with ipilimumab, and the lesion dimension. In particular, the DT classified patients with BRAF "wild-type" status having only 10.7% probability to reach complete/partial response. Among these lesions, those treated with doses < 24 Gy had 0% probability of complete/partial response. By contrast, lesions with a BRAF "mutated" status reported a probability of complete/partial response of 39.1%. Among these lesions, those treated with concomitant ipilimumab reached 100% probability of complete/partial response. Machine-learning models enable a reliable prediction of the treatment response of oligometastatic lesions receiving SBRT. This approach may assist radiation oncologists to tailor more individualized treatment plans in this clinical setting. An external validation of the results is mandatory.

papers.title: Implementation of a student pharmacist-led medication review program prior to metaiodobenzylguanidine (MIBG) imaging in pediatric oncology patients.
papers.abstract: IntroductionMetaiodobenzylguanidine (MIBG) imaging is a diagnostic and staging modality for patients with neuroblastoma and other neuroendocrine tumors. Commonly prescribed medications can interfere with MIBG uptake, resulting in nondiagnostic scans and treatment delays. Ensuring timely identification and discontinuation of interfering medications is essential, but it can be challenging within existing clinical pharmacy workloads. To reduce preventable scan delays and cancellations, a student pharmacist-led outreach process was developed. Student pharmacists have demonstrated value in medication reconciliation and patient outreach activities; however, their role in supporting MIBG imaging workflows has not been well described.MethodsThe primary objective was to determine the percentage of patients successfully contacted within three weeks of a scheduled MIBG scan. Secondary objectives included identifying interfering medications before imaging, characterizing outreach methods, contact attempts, and medication-related interventions. This retrospective observational study was implemented at St Jude Children's Research Hospital between October 1, 2024, and July 31, 2025, and subsequently evaluated retrospectively. Student pharmacists reviewed medication lists for patients scheduled for MIBG imaging, identified potential medication interactions, and conducted outreach using electronic health record (EHR)-integrated patient portal messaging and telephone communication.ResultsOf 139 patient appointments meeting inclusion criteria, 23 were initially identified as having interfering medications and were forwarded directly to providers without patient contact. Among 116 appointments eligible for outreach, 76 patients (65.5%) were successfully contacted within three weeks of the scheduled scan. Successful contacts occurred on the first (26.7%), second (24.4%), and third (64.6%) outreach attempts. The average number of contact attempts per patient was 2.1. Patient portal messaging accounted for most outreach attempts. Four additional interfering medications were identified through patient outreach, resulting in a total of 27 medication-related interventions.ConclusionsA student pharmacist-led MIBG medication review and outreach program, supported by EHR-based tools, successfully identified clinically significant medication interactions prior to scheduled imaging. This real-world experience expands the current literature by demonstrating the feasibility of integrating student pharmacists into specialized oncology workflows. This process helped to optimize imaging readiness, reduce the risk of costly scan delays or cancellations, and extend the reach of oncology pharmacy services. These findings support the use of student pharmacists as valuable clinical extenders within oncology practice models.
papers.journal: Journal of oncology pharmacy practice : official publication of the International Society of Oncology Pharmacy Practitioners

papers.title: Mixed adeno-neuroendocrine neoplasm (MiNEN) of the small intestine presenting as sub-occlusive syndrome: a rare and challenging diagnosis.
papers.abstract: Mixed neuroendocrine-non-neuroendocrine neoplasms (MiNENs) are rare gastrointestinal tumors characterized by the coexistence of a neuroendocrine and a non-neuroendocrine component within the same lesion, each representing ≥30% of the tumor volume according to the 2019 WHO classification. Diagnosis remains challenging due to nonspecific symptoms, clinical variability, and limitations of imaging and biopsy sampling. MiNENs of the small intestine are particularly rare, and presentation as subocclusive syndrome is uncommon. We report the case of a 72-year-old patient admitted with a three-day history of subocclusive syndrome. Clinical examination revealed a diffusely tender abdomen without peritonitis, and laboratory tests were within normal limits. CT imaging showed an organic small-bowel obstruction upstream of extensive inflammatory-appearing jejunal thickening. Exploratory laparotomy revealed a stenosing jejunal mass located 40 cm from the duodenojejunal flexure, associated with multiple mesenteric lymph nodes. Segmental resection with termino-terminal anastomosis was performed. Histopathology identified a MiNEN composed of a moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma and a neuroendocrine carcinoma, classified as pT3N0Mx, with tumor-free margins. This case highlights the diagnostic difficulty with MiNENs, which are often mistaken for single-component tumors due to low biopsy sensitivity and the absence of specific radiological features. Diagnosis is most frequently established from surgical specimens. Management relies primarily on complete resection for localized disease, while adjuvant therapy is guided by the most aggressive tumor component. The rarity and aggressiveness of MiNENs require a multidisciplinary approach, as well as the publication of additional cases to enhance understanding of their biological behavior and to optimize therapeutic strategies.
papers.journal: International journal of surgery case reports

papers.title: Cervical lymph node metastasis of neuroendocrine carcinoma of unknown primary origin: a rare case report and review of the literature.
papers.abstract: Cervical lymph node metastases from a neuroendocrine carcinoma (NEC) of unknown primary origin represent an exceptionally rare clinical entity, accounting for only 3%-5% of all carcinomas of unknown primary origin. Due to their aggressive biological behavior and the absence of standardized clinical guidelines, they pose significant diagnostic and therapeutic dilemmas. A 28-year-old male with unremarkable medical, family, and social histories presented with a rapidly growing, painless, right-sided neck swelling of 8 months' duration. Fine-needle aspiration cytology was inconclusive. A diagnostic adenectomy suggested a poorly differentiated neuroendocrine neoplasm. Extensive whole-body imaging, including a CT scan, an OctreoScan, and subsequent upper and lower gastrointestinal endoscopies, failed to reveal a primary source. The patient underwent a right-sided radical neck dissection due to extensive local infiltration, followed by adjuvant chemotherapy consisting of cisplatin and etoposide. At the 12-month follow-up, the patient remains in complete clinical and radiological remission. High-grade (grade III) cervical NECs require systematic exclusion of primary tumors, particularly from the bronchopulmonary tract, gastrointestinal tract, and thyroid gland. Immunohistochemical profiling is paramount; our case demonstrated positivity for synaptophysin, chromogranin, and CD56, with a Ki-67 index of 40%. Management must be aggressive and multidisciplinary, combining radical surgical clearance with platinum-based systemic chemotherapy to optimize locoregional control. Cervical high-grade NEC of unknown primary origin requires an exhaustive diagnostic workup and immunohistochemical evaluation. Early management via radical surgical resection and adjuvant systemic chemotherapy offers favorable locoregional control and survival outcomes.

papers.title: Small intestinal neuroendocrine tumor: a case report and literature review.
papers.abstract: Small intestinal neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) are rare neuroendocrine neoplasms, often asymptomatic or associated with functional carcinoid syndrome. Diagnosis is based on biochemical markers (urinary 5-HIAA, chromogranin A) and imaging studies. Management includes surgical resection and, in metastatic cases, somatostatin analogues and targeted therapies. A 52-year-old male with a history of appendectomy for acute simple appendicitis presented with sub-occlusive symptoms, including intermittent vomiting and diffuse abdominal pain without signs of peritonitis. Laboratory findings revealed elevated chromogranin A levels (140 ng/mL). Abdominopelvic CT identified an early ileal obstruction with an associated mesenteric mass and retractile mesenteritis, suggestive of an NET. The patient underwent ileocecal resection with mesenteric mass excision. Postoperative recovery was uneventful. Histopathological analysis confirmed the diagnosis of a NET. NETs, most commonly found in the small intestine, are often asymptomatic or present with complications such as obstruction. Diagnosis relies on chromogranin A and 5-HIAA tests, with imaging showing retractile mesenteritis. Treatment involves surgical resection for localized tumors and somatostatin analogs or radiotherapy for metastatic cases. This case underscores the diagnostic challenges posed by small bowel NETs due to their nonspecific clinical presentation. It highlights the value of integrating biochemical markers and imaging in diagnosis and confirms that timely surgical management can lead to favorable outcomes.
papers.journal: International journal of surgery case reports

papers.title: Identifying tumor microenvironment subtypes in pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors using digital spatial profiling.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to systematically investigate the heterogeneity and correlations between variables within the tumor microenvironment (TME) of primary and metastatic pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (PanNETs) using digital spatial profiling. Data from 63 PanNET patients were analyzed, and two distinct sample cohorts were selected for in-depth evaluation. Based on the composition and density of infiltrating immune cells and stromal characteristics, three distinct TME subtypes were identified: T1 (deficient, D), T2 (immune-enriched, IE), and T3 (immune- and fibroblast-enriched, IE/F). The three TME subtypes exhibited distinct clinical prognostic significance, with subtype T3 (IE/F) being associated with the lowest overall survival rates, particularly in metastatic disease (MT3). Molecular characterization revealed substantial variations in gene and protein expression profiles among the subtypes. We further developed an eight-gene prognostic model specifically for identifying MT3 (IE/F), which demonstrated enhanced accuracy for predicting patient survival compared to conventional pathological grading systems. These findings provide critical insights into the complexities of TME and offer a potential framework for personalized treatment strategies for PanNET patients.
