papers.title: Belzutifan as a possible novel treatment for sporadic central nervous system hemangioblastoma: a report of two cases and focused review of the literature.
papers.abstract: To provide a review of hemangioblastoma treatment and to report a new treatment option for sporadic, non-von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) associated central nervous system hemangioblastomas (CNS-HBs). Belzutifan is FDA-approved for the treatment of VHL associated cancers including renal cell carcinoma, pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors and CNS-HBs as a hypoxia-inducible factor-2α inhibitor. The efficacy of belzutifan is unclear for sporadic, non-vHL associated CNS-HBs, a disease entity with limited systemic options. A 23-year-old female presented with a posterior fossa hemangioblastoma which was then resected. At initial recurrence, she completed fractionated radiation therapy with a positive radiographic response. She had multiple symptomatic radiographic recurrences that underwent additional resection. After her fourth recurrence, surgery as well as radiation were not felt to be a reasonable option. Belzutifan 120 mg daily was started. Two months later, she had radiographic improvement with reduction in size of the posterior fossa hemangioblastoma, which has been maintained after 24 months of treatment. A second case is a 33-year-old male with a C7-T1 non-vHL hemangioblastoma that was resected and radiated at recurrence. Nine years later, the patient had radiographic progression that was not amenable to surgery or radiation. Belzutifan was started, which resulted in radiographic and subjective symptomatic improvement. We present two cases of sporadic recurrent hemangioblastoma with radiographic improvement to belzutifan, along with a review of hemangioblastoma treatment. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first two cases of radiographic improvement in sporadic, non-VHL associated CNS-HB from the use of belzutifan.

papers.title: Development of a Genetically Characterized Panel of 15 Mucosal Melanoma Cell Lines for the Preclinical Evaluation of Targeted Therapies in Human and Veterinary Medicine.
papers.abstract: Mucosal melanoma (MM) is a rare and aggressive cancer in humans, with limited therapeutical options and no faithful models for preclinical research. Interestingly, this malignancy occurs spontaneously and with higher frequency in certain dog breeds, due to artificial selection contributing to predisposition to specific melanoma subtypes. Owing to the strong genetic and clinical similarities between canine and human cancers, the dog represents a powerful model in the context of comparative oncology. We genetically characterized a panel of 15 canine mucosal melanoma cell lines exploring the main mutations and copy number variants and showed that the main genetic alterations are the same as in human MM. We then evaluated the in vitro responses to anticancer agents and identified relevant correlations between genomic alterations and drug sensitivity. Idasanutlin, an MDM2 inhibitor, showed the most promising and specific responses across the panel, with sensitivity closely associated with TP53 mutational status. After validating tumorigenicity of each cell line, two of them, presenting contrasted sensitivities in vitro, demonstrated their respective resistant and sensitive profiles in in vivo murine xenografts. This work highlights the value of this canine mucosal melanoma cell lines panel, harboring different genetic alterations, recapitulating the main genetic alterations seen in human and canine MM. We thus provide here a relevant tool for preclinical drug testing, and we demonstrate the value of canine mucosal melanoma as a translational model for comparative oncology (see graphical abstract).

papers.title: Preclinical Models of Uveal Melanoma: Strengths, Limitations, and Translational Utility.
papers.abstract: Uveal melanoma (UM) is the most common primary intraocular malignancy in adults and is characterized by a high propensity for metastatic dissemination, particularly to the liver, which remains largely incurable. Despite advances in the molecular characterization of UM, progress in therapeutic development has been limited, in part due to the lack of preclinical models that faithfully recapitulate the biological complexity and clinical behavior of the disease. A wide range of in vitro and in vivo systems have been developed, including primary cultures and established cell lines, three-dimensional (3D) cultures, patient-derived organoids (PDOs), xenografts, and genetically engineered animal models. Each of these models captures specific aspects of UM biology but also presents inherent limitations related to genetic drift, microenvironmental context, immune interactions, and metastatic fidelity. In this review, we provide an overview of current preclinical models used to study UM, with a focus on the strengths and limitations of each system. We also discuss emerging strategies to improve model fidelity and translational relevance. Continued development of integrated and physiologically relevant models will be essential to bridge the gap between discovery and clinical application in UM.

papers.title: EpiTIL: methylation tumor infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) predictor associates with survival in primary melanoma.
papers.abstract: Melanomas are immunogenic with significant variation of tumor infiltrating lymphocytes (TIL). Primary melanomas are routinely scored by pathologists, for TIL grade, as brisk, nonbrisk, and absent, but TIL grade is not utilized in staging. While brisk TIL grade predicts improved melanoma-specific survival, nonbrisk TIL grade often lacks prognostic significance. A high proportion of primary melanomas from stage II and III patients are scored as nonbrisk TIL grade. Our goal is to quantitatively predict T cell estimates in primary melanoma from DNA methylation data using immunofluorescence CD3 + staining as ground truth. Primary cutaneous melanomas (n = 80), analyzed for multiplex-immunofluorescence (CD3, CD8, S100) and whole-genome DNA methylation, underwent elastic net modeling of the proportion of CD3 + T lymphocytes to build a quantitative prediction model for TILs in primary melanoma called EpiTIL. Melanoma-specific survival (MSS) Kaplan-Meier curves significantly differed by primary melanoma EpiTIL tertiles (p = 0.001). Patients with intermediate or highest tertile EpiTIL scores had higher median probability of MSS than those with lowest tertile scores. EpiTIL added significant prognostic value for MSS beyond age, sex, and stage, analyzed using proportional hazard regression modelling (p = 0.012). EpiTIL survival prediction was validated in two multi-omic studies, TCGA (n = 352) and InterMEL (n = 399). Among TCGA melanomas, the survival curves significantly differed by EpiTIL tertile scores (p = 0.009) and EpiTIL scores added prognostic value to clinical factors (p < 0.002). In the InterMEL case-control study of stage II/III melanoma, patients with 5-year MSS without recurrence (controls) had a significantly higher mean EpiTIL scores than those who died of melanoma within 5 years (cases) (p = 1.5e - 11). Using logistic regression, EpiTIL scores significantly predicted 5-year MSS without recurrence, even after adjusting for age, sex, stage and TIL grade, with OR = 4.7 (p = 2.38e-06) comparing the highest to lowest EpiTIL tertiles. Extending the EpiTIL prediction to the Newell metastatic melanoma cohort, we found immune checkpoint inhibitor responders had a significantly higher mean EpiTIL score than non-responders (p = 0.047). EpiTIL is a DNA methylation-based predictor of T cell proportion that demonstrates potential prognostic value in primary melanoma, particularly for stages II and III. Furthermore, higher EpiTIL scores derived from primary melanomas were positively associated with improved therapeutic responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors in metastatic disease, highlighting its potential to identify patients most likely to benefit from immunotherapy.

papers.title: Neuroendocrine neoplasms of the digestive system: challenges of biopsy diagnosis.
papers.abstract: The diagnosis of digestive neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) is increasingly being made on endoscopic biopsies and endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration/biopsy (EUS-FNA/FNB) or ultrasound biopsies taken from metastases. Although current classification systems provide a robust and elaborate framework for categorizing NENs, their application to limited tissue biopsy samples often remains challenging. A major challenge is the accurate distinction between well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) and poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinomas (NECs), which is essential because of their markedly different prognostic and therapeutic implications. Additional challenges include reliable Ki-67 assessment, recognition of intratumoral heterogeneity, and identification of mixed neoplasms, including mixed neuroendocrine-non-neuroendocrine neoplasms (MiNENs) and amphicrine-like carcinoma (ALC)-a recently introduced and still poorly characterized category-and assignment of the primary site in metastatic disease using organ-associated immunohistochemical markers. Site-specific differences in morphology and immunophenotype further complicate biopsy interpretation and require integration of histological, immunohistochemical, clinical, and radiological findings. Although morphology remains the cornerstone of diagnosis, molecular testing is increasingly used in difficult cases to identify predictive biomarkers and potentially actionable genomic alterations. This review focuses on a practical biopsy-oriented diagnostic approach, discusses major diagnostic pitfalls, controversial and emerging concepts, and highlights the clinicopathological features of NENs across the digestive tract.
papers.journal: Virchows Archiv : an international journal of pathology

papers.title: Melanoma and Subungual Melanoma of the Hand.
papers.abstract: Subungual melanoma, a subtype of acral lentiginous melanoma, and nonacral melanomas of the hand differ in etiology, epidemiology, pathology, and treatment. Clinically, melanomas of the hand may have a variety of clinical manifestations, including a pigmented lesion under the nail, a melanotic lesion on the volar or dorsal hand, or amelanotic melanoma. It is critical for hand surgeons to understand clinical features that make a lesion concerning for malignant melanoma and to have a low threshold to biopsy concerning lesions.

papers.title: Nonmelanoma Skin Cancer of the Hand.
papers.abstract: Nonmelanoma skin cancers of the hand are a diverse group of tumors that share certain risk factors, including chronic ultraviolet light exposure, immunosuppression, age over 60, male gender, and light skin phototypes. The 2 most common include squamous cell carcinoma, which is also the most common primary skin cancer of the hand, and basal cell carcinoma, which is the most common skin cancer overall. This article discusses the histopathology, clinical features, and recommended surgical management for these 4 most common nonmelanoma skin cancers. The goal of treatment is to preserve hand function while achieving negative surgical margins.

papers.title: Controversies in NEN: An ENETS position statement on the diagnosis and treatment of mixed neuroendocrine/non-neuroendocrine neoplasms of the digestive system.
papers.abstract: Mixed neuroendocrine/non-neuroendocrine neoplasms (MiNEN) of the digestive system are rare epithelial malignancies characterised by the coexistence of neuroendocrine and non-neuroendocrine neoplasm components within the same lesion, where each component must account for at least 30% of the total tumour cell population. Despite growing recognition, MiNEN remain diagnostically and therapeutically challenging because of marked morphological heterogeneity, biological plasticity, and limited evidence guiding management. Recent molecular studies support a common clonal origin with subsequent divergent differentiation, although the mechanisms underlying progression and treatment resistance remain incompletely understood. This ENETS position statement summarises current evidence and expert opinion regarding the diagnosis and treatment of digestive MiNEN, focusing on major controversies in pathology, molecular biology, imaging, and management. Key diagnostic issues include the arbitrary 30% cutoff defining MiNEN, sampling limitations in biopsy specimens, intra-tumoural heterogeneity, and the distinction between amphicrine and collision neoplasms. Molecular profiling increasingly demonstrates shared genomic alterations between distinct components and may identify potentially actionable targets, including high level of microsatellite instability (MSI-high) or deficient mismatch repair (dMMR) and V-RAF murine sarcoma viral oncogene homolog B1 (BRAF) alterations in selected cases. Clinical management should be individualised according to anatomical site, stage, differentiation and proliferation of each component, and the histology of metastatic disease when available. Surgery is the main potentially curative approach for localised resectable disease. Perioperative and metastatic systemic treatments are extrapolated predominantly from site-specific adenocarcinoma and poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinoma (NEC) practice; no regimen has been prospectively established as superior specifically for MiNEN. Given the rarity and complexity of MiNEN, multidisciplinary management in expert centres, centralised pathological review, and international collaborative registries are essential to improve diagnostic standardisation and optimise treatment strategies.

papers.title: Stage-dependent management paradigms for MEN1-related Zollinger-Ellison syndrome: A vignette-based study by the ENETS MEN1 Task Force across 57 expert centers.
papers.abstract: Management of Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (ZES) in patients with multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1) remains controversial, particularly in non-metastatic disease where the role of surgery is debated. In contrast, treatment of metastatic disease is guided by established systemic approaches. We aimed to evaluate stage-dependent clinical decision-making in MEN1-related ZES using standardized clinical vignettes across ENETS Centers of Excellence (CoEs). A questionnaire-based study using two clinical vignettes was conducted by the ENETS MEN1 Task Force across all 68 ENETS CoEs, with a predefined participation target of 70%. Additional non-ENETS expert centers were also invited. Dedicated multidisciplinary teams provided institutional consensus responses. Scenarios included non-metastatic disease, locally metastatic disease, and distant metastatic disease. Centers were stratified by volume using a cutoff of 30 MEN1 patients in active care. Data were analyzed descriptively, comparing management strategies between low- and high-volume centers. Fifty-seven centers participated (52 of 68 ENETS CoEs [76.5%] and 5 additional non-ENETS expert centers). All 57 centers completed the questionnaire in full. All cases received symptomatic therapy with proton pump inhibitors. In non-metastatic disease, management was heterogeneous, with 56.1% recommending surgery. Centre volume strongly influenced decisions (73.1% vs. 41.9% surgery in low- vs. high-volume centers, p = .018). Preferred surgical approaches included duodenotomy with regional lymphadenectomy (43.9%) and the Thompson procedure (left pancreatectomy, duodenal exploration with excision of tumors and node dissection, enucleation of pancreatic head lesions; 26.3%). In locally metastatic disease, surgical management increased to 78.9%, with a shift toward more extensive procedures including pancreaticoduodenectomy (35.1%). In distant metastatic disease, somatostatin analogues were the systemic therapy of choice (50.9%), followed by curative-intent surgery with pancreaticoduodenectomy or duodenotomy with regional lymphadenectomy combined with liver resection or thermal ablation of liver lesions (35.1%), while no other systemic treatments were selected by any center. A liver biopsy was recommended by 43.9% of centers. Management of MEN1-related ZES demonstrates stage-dependent convergence. In early disease, decision-making-particularly regarding surgical versus medical management-is highly variable and influenced by center experience, whereas advanced disease shows more consistent, guideline-aligned treatment patterns. The high participation rate across ENETS CoEs suggests that these findings are likely to be relevant to expert neuroendocrine tumor practice.

papers.title: Primary cauda equina neuroendocrine tumor mimicking myxopapillary ependymoma: illustrative case.
papers.abstract: Primary cauda equina neuroendocrine tumors (CENETs) are rare intradural extramedullary neoplasms that were historically termed cauda equina paragangliomas. They may resemble more common cauda equina lesions, including myxopapillary ependymoma and schwannoma, on preoperative imaging. Recent molecular and immunohistochemical studies support CENET as a distinct entity, creating a need for practical diagnostic frameworks that separate primary tumors from metastatic neuroendocrine disease and nonneuroendocrine mimics. A 42-year-old woman presented with progressive nocturnal low back pain, bilateral leg heaviness, lower extremity numbness, and urinary incontinence. MRI demonstrated a 5-cm L1-3 intradural extramedullary mass nearly occupying the spinal canal, with cauda equina compression and prominent surrounding vessels. She underwent urgent L1-3 laminoplasty and microsurgical resection. Intraoperatively, the tumor was extremely vascular, friable, and associated with the filum terminale. Gross-total resection was achieved. Pathology demonstrated a WHO grade 1 primary CENET with neuroendocrine marker expression, CK8/18 positivity, low proliferative index, and no evidence of systemic neuroendocrine malignancy on postoperative staging. Cauda equina neuroendocrine lesions should be approached as a diagnostic spectrum. Clinical tempo, lesion multiplicity, imaging clues, intraoperative vascularity, and immunohistochemical/molecular workup can help distinguish primary CENET from metastatic neuroendocrine disease and mimics. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26609.

papers.title: Primary Small Cell Carcinoma of the Thyroid With Absent Calcitonin Expression: A Diagnostic Challenge.
papers.abstract: Primary small cell carcinoma of the thyroid is an exceedingly rare and aggressive neuroendocrine malignancy. Diagnosis may be particularly challenging in tumors lacking calcitonin expression, in which distinction from medullary thyroid carcinoma and metastatic neuroendocrine carcinomas is required. A 50-year-old woman presented with progressive hoarseness and a rapidly enlarging cervical mass. Imaging revealed a highly infiltrative thyroid tumor with multiple cervical lymphadenopathies and no evidence of a primary tumor elsewhere. Serum calcitonin levels were within normal limits. Fine-needle aspiration biopsy of the thyroid lesion and a cervical lymph node demonstrated cytologic features consistent with small cell carcinoma. Following a good response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy, total thyroidectomy with central, bilateral mediastinal lymphadenectomy was performed. Histologic examination demonstrated a highly infiltrative neoplasm composed of small cells arranged in solid and nested patterns with marked mitotic activity, tumor necrosis, and vascular and perineural invasion. Tumor cells expressed neuroendocrine markers with focal positivity for TTF-1/NKX2-1 and CEA, while calcitonin, thyroglobulin, PAX8, and CGRP were negative. Primary thyroid small cell carcinoma is exceptionally rare and its histogenesis remains uncertain. Diagnosis requires careful clinicopathologic correlation and exclusion of metastatic disease and calcitonin-negative variants of medullary thyroid carcinoma.

papers.title: Safety, recovery, and hospital resource use after robot-assisted pheochromocytoma resection in a 48-hour short-stay pathway: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: To compare perioperative safety, early recovery, and resource use between a short-stay pathway and conventional inpatient care for robot-assisted pheochromocytoma resection. This single-center retrospective cohort included 110 patients who underwent robot-assisted pheochromocytoma resection: 47 managed in a short-stay pathway with discharge planned within 48 h of hospital admission and 63 managed with conventional inpatient care during the same period. The primary outcome was a 30-day composite of Clavien-Dindo grade II or higher complications, unplanned intensive care, emergency attendance, readmission, reoperation, or death. Secondary outcomes included intraoperative hemodynamic instability, postoperative hypotension and hypoglycemia, pain, opioid consumption, Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15), length of stay, costs, pathway completion, and patient satisfaction. Welch t tests and Fisher exact tests were used for unadjusted comparisons, and absolute risk differences (RDs) and mean differences are reported with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Exploratory linear models with heteroscedasticity-robust standard errors adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, ASA class, tumor size, and duration of alpha blockade; sensitivity analyses additionally adjusted for surgeon, surgical approach, secretory phenotype, and hypertension. Baseline, comorbidity, endocrine, and operative characteristics were similar between groups (all standardized mean differences < 0.30). The 30-day composite safety outcome occurred in 1 of 47 short-stay patients (2.1%) and 1 of 63 conventional inpatients (1.6%; RD 0.5% points, 95% CI -6.6 to 9.6; P = 1.000). Intraoperative hemodynamic instability was also similar (83.0% vs. 87.3%; P = 0.590), as were persistent postoperative hypotension (8.5% vs. 7.9%) and postoperative hypoglycemia (8.5% vs. 7.9%). The planned 48-hour discharge target was achieved in 44 of 47 patients (93.6%). Compared with conventional care, the short-stay pathway had lower 24-hour pain scores (mean 1.8 vs. 2.4), total inpatient opioid exposure (8.7 vs. 17.7 mg morphine milligram equivalents), postoperative stay (44.2 vs. 105.1 h), total stay (49.2 vs. 476.4 h), and total in-hospital cost (CNY 49,858 vs. CNY 64,802), with higher 24-hour QoR-15 (119.7 vs. 107.9) and satisfaction (9.2 vs. 8.2); these differences remained significant after Holm correction and were consistent in fully adjusted sensitivity analyses. Among selected patients undergoing robot-assisted pheochromocytoma resection, the short-stay pathway was associated with similar observed perioperative safety outcomes, faster recovery, shorter hospitalization, lower in-hospital costs, and higher patient satisfaction than conventional inpatient care. Because only two composite events occurred and the 95% CI of the risk difference was wide, these findings provide preliminary evidence of feasibility rather than proof of equivalent safety, and support prospective validation.

papers.title: A Red Blood Cell-Hitchhiking Dendrimer Nanovaccine Potentiates Antitumor Immunity via Lymphoid Organ Targeting.
papers.abstract: Efficient antigen delivery to antigen-presenting cells remains a critical challenge in cancer nanovaccine development. In this study, we develop a dendrimer-based nanovaccine (DenV) for efficient tumor treatment and prevention via a red blood cell (RBC) hitchhiking strategy. Utilizing phenylboronic acid-grafted dendrimers, model antigen ovalbumin (OVA) and immune adjuvant CpG oligodeoxynucleotide (CpG ODN) can be efficiently co-loaded to get DenV with a relatively simple fabrication process. Upon further RBC anchoring, DenV@RBC demonstrates a distinct application feature from DenV with a desired delivery profile to lymphoid organs. In vivo antitumor results in a mouse subcutaneous melanoma model show that both DenV and DenV@RBC achieve excellent antitumor effects following systemic administration, where the therapeutic efficacy of DenV@RBC is slightly superior to that of DenV. Meanwhile, DenV and DenV@RBC allow excellent tumor-preventive effects, regardless of local or systematic administration routes. It is also found that DenV is more robust upon local injection, while DenV@RBC yields better tumor prevention performance when administered systemically via the bloodstream. Our study offers a dendrimer-based strategy with interaction to natural RBCs for the development of highly efficient nanovaccines and holds substantial application potential in the field of cancer immunotherapy.

papers.title: Bilateral pheochromocytoma and multiple paragangliomas in a patient with a heterozygous SDHD mutation: A challenging case report.
papers.abstract: Hereditary pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma (PPGL) are rare, genetically determined neuroendocrine tumors that often present at a young age. Their multifocal nature poses diagnostic and therapeutic challenges and warrants early genetic testing. A 26-year-old man was referred for cervical and mediastinal paragangliomas. Computed tomography scan revealed multiple cervical and mediastinal paragangliomas and bilateral pheochromocytoma. Plasma normetanephrine was 2616 ng/L (13 times the upper normal limit). Genetic testing confirmed an SDHD mutation. After alpha- and beta-blockade, the patient underwent bilateral adrenalectomy and mediastinal paraganglioma resection under cardiopulmonary bypass. Octreotide therapy was initiated due to inoperability of cervical paragangliomas.However, a loss of therapeutic response was observed one year after the initiation of somatostatin analogue. Radiotherapy was then considered for the cervical paragangliomas. This case underlines the complexity of PPGL management in patients with SDHD mutation. Multifocal disease demands individualized, multidisciplinary strategies and long-term follow-up to minimize morbidity and optimize outcomes in young patients.
papers.journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders

papers.title: Nanopore Sequencing Identifies a Distinct Tyr::CreERT2 Allele Circulating in Existing Mouse Stocks.
papers.abstract: The Tyr::CreERT2 transgenic mouse lines are essential tools for conditional gene manipulation in melanocytes and are widely used in melanoma research. Two independent lines are in common use, the Bosenberg line and the Larue line, with transgene integration sites for both characterized by whole genome sequencing. Precise knowledge of these sites is critical for designing complex genetic crosses. Here we report that a Tyr::CreERT2 mouse stock routinely used in BrafCA;Ptenflox melanoma models and associated with elevated spontaneous melanoma penetrance carries a previously undescribed integration on Chromosome 1, distinct from the previously reported Chromosome 2 integration. Using long-read Nanopore whole genome sequencing, we mapped the integration to an intergenic locus between Alppl2 and Alpi, revealing a 2431 bp genomic deletion at the insertion site. We developed position-specific junction PCR and qPCR assays to genotype this allele and confirmed that offspring are born at Mendelian ratios. This distinct integration may account for the elevated melanoma penetrance observed in this stock, with direct implications for the many laboratories employing this widely distributed model.

papers.title: Metastatic insulinoma: clinical presentation, management, and outcomes. A systematic review.
papers.abstract: Metastatic insulinoma is a rare and clinically challenging entity for which an integrated, individual patient-level synthesis of clinical features, therapeutic strategies, and outcomes is lacking. We conducted a pre-registered systematic review of published case reports and case series reporting patients with metastatic insulinoma. Individual-level data were extracted from eligible studies identified through searches of four electronic databases from inception to January 2026. Survival analyses were performed using Kaplan-Meier estimation and Cox proportional hazards regression. The final cohort comprised 275 patients with individual-level data. Median age at diagnosis was 55 years (IQR 43-65); 54.9% were women. Among 260 patients with available timing data, metastatic disease was synchronous in 200 (76.9%) and metachronous in 60 (23.1%). The liver was the predominant metastatic site (89.5%), while 82.8% of patients (111/134 evaluable) required nutritional support, reflecting the profound endocrine and metabolic burden of the disease. Histopathological grading was available in 44.0% of patients, with G2 tumors predominating (56.2%) and a median Ki-67 of 5.7%. Surgery was performed in 61.3% (160/261 evaluable), with complete resection achieved in 10.6%. A disease control rate of 69.9% (153 evaluable) was observed with multimodal therapy, and definitive hypoglycemia control was achieved in 62.1% (164/264) of patients at last follow-up. Median overall survival from the time of metastatic diagnosis was 84 months (95% CI: 61.8-111), with a subset of patients surviving beyond 25 years. Patients with metachronous disease had superior overall survival compared with synchronous presentation (median not reached vs. 56.4 months; unadjusted HR 0.29, 95% CI 0.15-0.57; p < 0.001). This large, descriptive, individual patient-level synthesis of metastatic insulinoma suggests that survival among published cases with extractable follow-up is heterogeneous and may be longer than earlier small series indicated, with a median overall survival approaching seven years and remarkable long-term survival in a subset of patients. The timing of metastatic presentation emerged as a potential prognostic factor, although this exploratory, unadjusted association requires further investigation. Overall, our findings support an individualized, multidisciplinary treatment strategy integrating endocrine, oncological, and interventional expertise.

papers.title: AB027. Paraneoplastic diseases in patients with thymic epithelial tumours: findings from the nation-wide Danish thymic epithelial tumor database.
papers.abstract: Patients with thymic epithelial tumors (TETs) are predisposed to autoimmune dis-eases, immunodeficiencies, and extrathymic malignancies. Still, the timing of these conditions relative to TET diagnosis and their prognostic significance remain poorly characterized. This nationwide study included all Danish patients diagnosed with TETs from 2015 to 2020. Data on demographics, tumor subtype, autoimmune diseases, immunodeficiencies, malig-nancies, follow-up, and survival were collected from electronic medical records. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize patient characteristics and disease chronology, while Kaplan-Meier analyses and log-rank tests were applied to assess associating with survival. Among 282 patients with a median age of 66 years, thymoma accounted for 85% of cases, thymic carcinoma for 14%, and thymic neuroendocrine tumors for 1.4%. Prior to TET diagnosis, 105 (37.2%) patients had a previous cancer diagnosis and 88 (31.2%) had autoim-mune disease. Over a median follow-up of 65 months, 33 (11.7%) patients developed new auto-immune diseases, and 41 (14.5%) patients developed new extrathymic cancers. The pattern of malignancies differed over time, with skin and colorectal cancers predominating before TET diagnosis, while lymphoma and prostate cancer were most frequent afterward. Myasthenia gravis was the leading autoimmune disease both before and after TET diagnosis, while Good's syndrome occurred only after diagnosis in six patients. Pre-existing autoimmune disease and pre-existing extrathymic cancer were not significantly associated with overall survival. A substantial burden of autoimmune and malignant disease was observed among patients with TETs, predominated by myasthenia gravis. Pre-existing paraneoplastic diseases were not associated with survival. A trend was observed in the incidence of certain disorders suggesting a shift in the pattern of developed paraneoplastic diseases after TET diagnosis.

papers.title: Typical Carcinoid Tumor of the Lung: A Case Report Demonstrating Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results Database Analysis.
papers.abstract: Typical lung carcinoid tumors are classified as well-differentiated, low-grade (G1) neuroendocrine neoplasms. This case study details the clinical course, diagnostic complexity, and definitive management of a 41-year-old African American male diagnosed with a histologically confirmed typical carcinoid (G1) that manifested a highly aggressive anatomical phenotype. Key features included bulky multi-station ipsilateral mediastinal lymph node metastasis (N2 disease), prevalent lymphovascular invasion, and direct phrenic nerve involvement. Following definitive surgical resection (left upper lobe segmentectomy), the disease was pathologically staged as pT2a N2 M0 (Stage IIIA).

papers.title: Association of fatty acid binding protein 4 with altered immune composition and ferroptosis related signatures in metastatic medullary thyroid cancer.
papers.abstract: Medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) has a relatively poor prognosis mainly attributed to its early metastasis. This study aimed to investigate the expression pattern of fatty acid binding protein 4 (FABP4) and its relationship to the immune and metabolic landscape in metastatic MTC. Tissues for single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis were obtained from Jurong Hospital, to reveal the immune landscape of metastatic MTC. Gene expression profiles from Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) were analyzed through weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), differential expression gene (DEG) analysis and functional enrichment. Tissues for immunohistochemistry (IHC) were from The First Affiliated Hospital with Nanjing Medical University. scRNA-seq showed that the lymph node cellular composition diverged from that of primary tissues, with an increased proportions of B cells versus T/natural killer cells. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) revealed substantial enrichment pathways including fatty acid metabolism. After discriminating tumor cells by inferCNV and CopyKAT, FABP4 was more enriched in metastatic than in primary tumor cells, which was in line with IHC staining. Also, the module incorporating the six key genes including FABP4, which were found to be upregulated in metastatic MTC by DEGs with WGCNA. Functional enrichment displayed that the differential genes were associated with ferroptosis and fatty acid metabolism. The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) data presented the correlation between FABP4 and glutathione peroxidase 4. Elevated FABP4 expression is associated with metastatic MTC, concurrent with altered immune cell composition and enrichment of ferroptosis related pathways. These findings identified FABP4 as a potential biomarker of metastasis, which is useful for the completement of theoretical basis and the guidance of personalized therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: A retrospective analysis of TACE-based multimodal liver-directed therapy for unresectable gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine carcinoma with liver metastases.
papers.abstract: Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) is widely used for liver metastases from well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors, which are typically hypervascular. In contrast, gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine carcinoma liver metastases (GEP-NECLM) may be less hypervascular, raising uncertainty regarding the role of embolization-based therapy in this population. Nevertheless, TACE has also demonstrated antitumor activity in relatively hypovascular liver metastases, such as colorectal liver metastases. In clinical practice, TACE may also be combined with hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (HAIC) as part of a multimodal liver-directed strategy. We therefore hypothesized that TACE-based multimodal liver-directed therapy could provide intrahepatic antitumor activity in patients with unresectable GEP-NECLM and aimed to evaluate its efficacy, safety, and prognostic factors. Patients with unresectable GEP-NECLM who underwent TACE-based multimodal liver-directed therapy between February 2012 and June 2024 were retrospectively reviewed. Pathological diagnoses were reassessed according to the 2019 World Health Organization classification. The primary endpoint was overall survival (OS), defined as the time from the first TACE session to death from any cause. Secondary endpoints included progression-free survival (PFS), defined as the time from the first TACE session to progressive disease in any organ or all-cause mortality; hepatic progression-free survival (hPFS), defined as the time from the first TACE session to intrahepatic disease progression or all-cause mortality; objective response rate (ORR), disease control rate (DCR), and safety. A total of 34 patients were included; 24 (70.6%) received TACE in combination with HAIC, and 29 (85.3%) had received at least one line of prior systemic therapy. The ORR and DCR were 41.2% and 76.5%, respectively. After a median follow-up of 45.1 months, the median PFS was 4.4 months, the median hPFS was 5.5 months and the median OS was 10.8 months. Colorectal primary site was independently associated with shorter PFS, with a hazard ratio (HR) of 3.189 (P=0.01). Ki-67 proliferation index (Ki-67) ≥55% (HR =6.172; P=0.006) was independently associated with worse OS. A total of 34 patients underwent 60 interventional treatment sessions. The treatment showed an acceptable safety profile, with no 30-day mortality or hepatic decompensation. Post-embolization syndrome was the most common treatment-emergent adverse event, occurring in 32 of 60 sessions (53.3%). All adverse events were manageable with symptomatic treatment. TACE-based multimodal liver-directed therapy was associated with measurable intrahepatic antitumor activity and an acceptable safety profile in patients with unresectable GEP-NECLM. Colorectal primary site was independently associated with shorter PFS, whereas a Ki-67 ≥55% was independently associated with worse OS. These findings require further validation in larger prospective studies.

papers.title: Diagnostic approaches for neuroendocrine tumors of unknown primary: the role of surgical exploration and advances in molecular profiling.
The elusive culprit: a renal neuroendocrine tumor unmasked by ectopic Cushing syndrome.
papers.abstract: The case provides insight into the diagnostics and management of ectopic Cushing syndrome caused by the ectopic adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) secretion by a primary renal neuroendocrine tumor (RenNET), an exceptionally rare cause of endogenous hypercortisolism.

papers.title: From risk factors to individualized prediction: development and internal validation of a machine learning model for early identification of postoperative pneumonia after lung cancer surgery.
papers.abstract: Postoperative pneumonia (POP) remains one of the most common infectious complications following lung cancer surgery and is associated with substantial morbidity. Although several risk factors for POP have been identified, clinically applicable approaches for early individualized risk stratification remain limited. This study aimed to develop and internally validate machine learning models for early prediction of POP using routinely available perioperative variables. In this prospective single-center cohort study, 258 consecutive patients undergoing pulmonary resection for non-small cell lung cancer or pulmonary carcinoid tumors were screened, of whom 200 were included in the final study cohort. POP was defined by newly developed postoperative radiographic abnormalities accompanied by clinical signs of infection requiring antibiotic therapy. Machine learning models, including logistic regression (LR), Naïve Bayes (NB), random forest (RF), and XGBoost (XGB), were developed to predict POP using demographic, clinical, laboratory, surgical, and postoperative day 1 radiographic variables. Model performance was assessed using nested leave-one-out cross-validation and quantified by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). A nomogram was constructed from the best-performing model to facilitate individualized risk estimation. Different decision thresholds were explored to evaluate clinically relevant trade-offs between sensitivity and specificity. POP occurred in 47 of 200 patients (23.5%), while no POP-related mortality was observed. LR demonstrated the best predictive performance (AUROC 0.701±0.070), followed by NB (0.698±0.103), RF (0.656±0.217), and XGB (0.589±0.179). The most influential predictors included advanced age, perioperative changes in C-reactive protein concentration (ΔCRP), elevated preoperative CRP levels, prolonged operative duration, and abnormal postoperative day 1 chest radiographic findings. At a decision threshold of 25%, the model correctly identified 25 of 47 POP cases (53.2%), whereas increasing the threshold to 32.5% reduced false-positive classifications from 42 to 24 at the expense of missing an additional four POP cases. Machine learning models based on routinely available perioperative variables enabled early individualized prediction of POP following lung cancer surgery. LR provided the best balance between predictive performance, stability, and interpretability, allowing the development of an interpretable nomogram for individualized risk estimation. The model may have potential to support risk-adapted postoperative surveillance and more efficient allocation of healthcare resources; however, external validation is required before clinical implementation.

papers.title: Pediatric gigantism due to ectopic growth hormone releasing hormone secretion from a metastatic bronchial neuroendocrine tumor.
papers.abstract: Pediatric gigantism due to ectopic secretion of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) is exceptionally rare. Most pediatric reports have involved pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors in the context of multiple endocrine neoplasia 1 (MEN1). We describe a female patient diagnosed at 9 years of age with a typical bronchial neuroendocrine tumor and subsequently found to have diffuse hepatic and skeletal metastases, accelerated linear growth, and acromegalic features. Evaluation demonstrated markedly elevated plasma GHRH, growth hormone, and insulin-like growth factor 1, with diffuse pituitary hyperplasia on magnetic resonance imaging and no discrete pituitary adenoma. Genetic testing for MEN1 was negative. Management required repeated surgery, first-generation somatostatin analogs, dopamine agonist therapy, pegvisomant, pasireotide, and peptide receptor radionuclide therapy with lutetium-177 DOTA-Tyr3-octreotate. Pasireotide achieved improved biochemical control, while peptide receptor radionuclide therapy contributed to long-term structural stability. After 23 years of follow-up, the patient remains clinically well with stable tumor burden and controlled somatotropic axis. This case highlights the natural history of a pediatric-onset GHRH-secreting neuroendocrine tumor and highlights the efficacy of aggressive, multidisciplinary management in achieving long-term survival.

papers.title: Prognostic prediction of pulmonary neuroendocrine carcinoma using a transformer-based artificial intelligence model: a two-center retrospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary neuroendocrine carcinomas (pNECs) are a rare and heterogeneous group of malignancies, ranging from low-grade carcinoids to high-grade small-cell lung carcinoma (SCLC) and large-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC). Prognostic tools for these tumors are scarce and have rarely been validated in external cohorts. This study aimed to develop a Transformer-based prognostic prediction model for pNEC and validate it in an independent external cohort, to improve survival estimation and support individualized treatment decisions. This retrospective two-center cohort study included 823 patients with surgically resected pNEC (2001-2023). Models were developed in Center 1 (n=374; randomly split 8:2 into training and internal test sets) and externally validated in an independent Center 2 cohort (n=449). Three algorithms-logistic regression (LR), decision tree (DT), and the Transformer-based tabular foundation model TabPFN-were compared for estimating overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) at 1-, 3-, and 5-year landmarks, with evaluation by receiver operating characteristic, calibration, and decision curve analyses, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis for interpretability. TabPFN achieved the highest area under the curve (AUC) in most tasks in both test sets, with task-dependent exceptions: in the internal test set, logistic regression performed best for 1-year OS (AUC 0.885), while TabPFN performed best for the remaining tasks, including 3-year OS (0.880), overall DFS (0.810), and 1-year DFS (0.892); in the external test set, TabPFN remained best for 1- and 3-year OS and for overall, 1-, and 3-year DFS (0.747-0.802), whereas logistic regression performed best for 5-year OS and DFS. External calibration was less satisfactory. Disease stage, pathological subtype, and age were the key prognostic predictors, and TabPFN was more accurate for low-grade subtypes. SHAP analysis quantified the contribution of each feature and made the model interpretable. The Transformer-based model improves survival estimation in pNEC, with task-dependent advantages over conventional methods and confirmed transportability to an independent institutional cohort. Prospective multicenter validation and calibration refinement are needed before broader clinical use.

papers.title: Central-type primitive neuroectodermal tumor of the uterus: Case report and literature review.
papers.abstract: Primitive neuroectodermal tumors (PNETs) arising in the uterus, particularly those classified as the central-type (cPNET), are exceedingly rare. To date, approximately 30 cases of uterine cPNET have been reported, and their clinicopathological features remain poorly characterized. These tumors typically present as highly aggressive small round cell neoplasms with variable neuroectodermal differentiation, often posing significant diagnostic challenges owing to their overlap with other uterine malignancies, including neuroendocrine carcinoma, endometrial stromal sarcoma, and undifferentiated carcinoma. Here, we report a rare case of uterine cPNET characterized by a diffuse small round cell morphology and prominent neuroendocrine differentiation. Immunohistochemical analysis demonstrated positivity for synaptophysin, INSM1, and CD56, whereas markers associated with Ewing's sarcoma (CD99, FLI1 and NKX2.2) were negative. Next-generation sequencing revealed no Ewing sarcoma breakpoint region 1 rearrangements, supporting the exclusion of peripheral PNET. This case highlights the diagnostic complexity of uterine tumors with neuroectodermal differentiation and expands the current morphological and immunophenotypic spectra of this entity. Accurate recognition requires the integration of histopathology, immunoprofile, and molecular findings, with particular attention paid to the differential diagnosis of other high-grade uterine malignancies.

papers.title: Gastric microbiota-mediated immune remodelling in gastric cancer.
Visualization of metabolic reprogramming of liver tumors in situ based on mass spectrometry imaging.
papers.abstract: Metabolic reprogramming, a hallmark of cancer, has the potential to create therapeutic vulnerabilities. Understanding and exploiting the metabolic differences between developing cancer cells and normal cells plays a crucial role in advancing cancer treatment. In the present study, utilizing temporal stable isotope labeling combined with mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) technology, spatial metabolic maps in the orthotopic liver cancer mouse model were obtained. This approach allowed us to simultaneously visualize the metabolic behavior of both cancerous and paracancerous tissues. Our results revealed a lower content of <sup>13</sup>C-labeled glucose in cancerous tissues compared with paracancerous tissues, together with the distinct isotope-associated signals of endogenous metabolites, including lactate, malate, glutamate, gluconate, and 11,12-epoxyeicosatrienoic acid (11,12-EET). Notably, the isotope-associated signals of lactate, malate, and glutamate were higher in cancerous tissue than in paracancerous tissue, whereas gluconate and 11,12-EET exhibited the opposite trend. These findings suggest a relatively active glycolysis pathway and TCA cycle, and relatively lower PPP-related glucose oxidation in cancerous tissues. Immunofluorescence analysis further characterized the expression patterns of related metabolic enzymes. This approach provides a powerful tool for visualizing the spatial and temporal regulation of metabolic dynamics in cancerous tissues, providing a unique opportunity to study the in situ metabolic reprogramming behavior of cancer.

papers.title: Targeted liquid biopsy using CEUS to facilitate the release of ctDNA in colorectal liver metastasis.
papers.abstract: Liquid biopsy as a non-invasive diagnosis tool for tumor genotyping, was limited by its low sensitivity. Ultrasound targeted microbubble destruction (UTMD) technique could temporarily alter tissue permeability, but its role in circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) released remains poor understood. This study included mouse experiments and a prospective clinical study, aimed to investigate whether UTMD could increase the release of ctDNA and thus enhance the sensitivity of liquid biopsy. To establish the safety profile, H&E staining, PCR and Flow cytometric assays were conducted to evaluate liver injury and tumor dissemination after UTMD treatment. To evaluate UTMD-induced ctDNA release, droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) was used to measure ctDNA copies at baseline and 5-30 min post-UTMD in BALB/c nude mice bearing liver metastases established with the human SW1463 colorectal cancer cell line (n = 28) and in patients with colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) (n = 10). In mouse models, UTMD under safety parameters (3∼3.3 MHz frequency, 2 cycles pulse length, 500 Hz PRF, 52.5%∼60% acoustic power and 0.5 MI) did not cause liver inflammation and tumor dissemination. UTMD treatment induced a transient, significant increase in human KRAS ctDNA copies (5-fold increase, P = 0.007), which returned to baseline within 30 min. In human participants with CRLM, sonication of the liver tumors resulted in a 2.2-fold increase (P = 0.045) in KRAS ctDNA mutant allele frequency measured 5 min after the procedure. These findings highlight the clinical utility of diagnostic ultrasound in liquid biopsy for detecting specific oncogene mutations in abdominal diseases, which are critical for personalized cancer therapy.

papers.title: Bacteroidetes promote hepatocellular carcinoma progression and resistance to immunotherapy.
papers.abstract:
Background and aims

Growing evidence highlights the gut microbiome's critical role in tumorigenesis and immunotherapy response. However, the impact of gut microbes on hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression and response to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) remains unclear due to the lack of combined preclinical and clinical studies.

Approach and results

We performed 16S rRNA sequencing of cross-cohort stool samples from 10 HCC responders (R) and 40 non-responders (NR) to ICB at baseline and on-treatment time points. We identified Bacteroidetes enrichment in NR. To study the microbiome's role in cancer immune response, we generated an immunogenic mouse model of HCC via hydrodynamic tail-vein injection (HDTVI) of DNA plasmids mimicking common HCC alterations and immunogenicity by expressing OVA model antigens (MYC-lucOS;CTNNB1 tumors). We found that antibiotic (ABX)-induced dysbiosis promoted a pro-tumorigenic effect in the MYC-lucOS;CTNNB1 HCC and reshaped the tumor immune microenvironment by reducing dendritic cells (DCs) through the expansion of the Bacteroidetes species, Parabacteroides distasonis. P. distasonis colonization in mice harboring MYC-lucOS;CTNNB1 liver tumors confirmed its pro-tumorigenic effect in vivo. Furthermore, fecal matter transplant of patient microbiotas into murine recipients demonstrated that microbiota from an NR donor enriched in Bacteroidetes promoted faster tumorigenesis compared with microbiota from an R donor with reduced Bacteroidetes. We isolated 6 Bacteroidetes species from the NR donor into a bacterial cocktail. After colonization with the Bacteroidetes cocktail, mice harboring MYC-lucOS;CTNNB1 HCC exhibited increased tumorigenesis, reduced survival, and impaired response to ICB.

Conclusions

This study identified Bacteroidetes enrichment as a potential biomarker of ICB resistance in HCC and, by using immunogenic mouse models, established that Bacteroidetes abundance influences tumor development and response to ICB.

papers.title: NBD-F derivatization and rapid separation of catecholamines and their O-methylated metabolites using flow-gated micellar electrokinetic chromatography.
papers.abstract: Catecholamines function as neurotransmitters and hormones in the brain and the sympathetic nervous system. Measurements of these compounds are important in neuroscience research, clinical diagnosis, and drug development. Their O-methylated metabolites, particularly metanephrine and normetanephrine, are established biomarkers used in the biochemical evaluation of pheochromocytomas and paragangliomas. The objective of this study was to evaluate 4-fluoro-7-nitro-2,1,3-benzoxadiazole (NBD-F) as the fluorogenic agent for the rapid separation and sensitive detection of these compounds using flow-gated capillary electrophoresis (CE). Experimental results showed that NBD-F in excess of the analytes readily reacted with amino and phenolic hydroxyl groups of catecholamines, resulting in fully NBD-substituted, tri-NBD derivatives. Similarly, the O-methylated metabolites of catecholamines were also fully NBD-substituted, forming di-NBD derivatives. These derivatives were separated with micellar electrokinetic chromatography (MEKC) within 80 s. Sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) in the sample solution might facilitate the derivatization of catecholamines, whereas SDS in the separation buffer enhanced fluorescence intensity of the derivatives. The limits of detection (LODs) were estimated to be 1.7 nM for dopamine and 1.3 nM for norepinephrine, representing an approximately 80-fold improvement over previously reported LODs obtained using the MEKC/NBD-Cl method. The method was further applied to the analysis of urine and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples to demonstrate its applicability. These results demonstrate the potential of the NBD-F/MEKC approach as a sensitive and rapid analytical method for catecholamines and their metabolites and as a useful biochemical tool for neuroscience research.

papers.title: Percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy for palliative oncology patients - a safety analysis in a retrospective cohort study.
papers.abstract:
Background

Patients with advanced cancer who are receiving palliative care represent a highly vulnerable population. The role of percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG) in this setting is controversial, particularly when life expectancy is limited. Our study aimed to assess complication rates following PEG placement in palliative oncology patients, as well as to compare outcomes with a non-palliative cohort. This comparison was made to identify safety signals that might argue against PEG placement in this population. Additionally, we aimed to evaluate the safety profiles of different PEG techniques.

Methods

In this retrospective cohort study, we analyzed patients who underwent PEG placement at the three endoscopic units of Charité - Universitätsmedizin Berlin between 2016 and 2021. Of these patients, 146 had advanced malignancy and were receiving palliative care. These patients were compared with 1.423 patients who underwent PEG placement in a non-palliative setting. Univariate- and multivariate analyses were performed to evaluate peri- and post-interventional complications. We present mortality data with a focus on PEG-related mortality.

Results

Overall complication rates did not differ significantly between palliative and non-palliative patients (37.0% vs. 32.3%; p = 0.246), while procedure-related mortality was higher in the palliative cohort (2.1% vs. 0.4% p = 0.013), although the number of events was small. In an additional analysis restricted to oncological patients, palliative status was not significantly associated with overall, peri-interventional, minor or major complications in multivariable models adjusted for age, sex, BMI, PEG placement technique, and PEG indication.

Conclusion

PEG placement in patients with advanced cancer who are receiving palliative care is not associated with significantly higher peri- or post-interventional complications compared to patients who are not receiving palliative care. Decisions regarding PEG placement should be made on a case-by-case basis, taking into account the clinical indication, anticipated benefits, patient preferences and procedural risks.

papers.title: Molecular mechanisms and biomarkers in glioma: recent advances and future perspectives.
papers.abstract: Gliomas are the most common primary tumors of the central nervous system, with high heterogeneity and aggressiveness. Recent advances have elucidated key molecular mechanisms in glioma pathogenesis, including dysregulation of the RTK/RAS/PI3K, p53, and RB pathways, alongside significant epigenetic alterations like IDH mutations and MGMT promoter methylation in tumorigenesis. In addition, biomarkers including 1p/19q codeletion and TERT promoter mutations have been incorporated into clinical trials to guide prognostic assessment and treatment decisions. IDH mutation status has additionally emerged as a predictive biomarker with direct therapeutic consequences, exemplified by the regulatory approval of vorasidenib for IDH-mutant grade 2 glioma. Furthermore, non-invasive liquid biopsy techniques, such as analysis of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)-derived circulating tumor DNA and exosomes, have emerged as promising tools for dynamic surveillance and early tumor detection. This review summarizes the progress of research into the molecular mechanisms of glioma, discusses potential diagnostic and therapeutic biomarkers, and looks ahead to future research directions.

papers.title: Novel Bifunctional PET Tracer 68Ga-DOTA-NI-FAPI-04 PET/CT in Gastrointestinal Tumors: An Exploratory Comparative Study With 18F-FDG.
papers.abstract:
Purpose

This study aims to evaluate the clinical feasibility of 68Ga-nitroimidazole-FAPI (NI-FAPI), targeting both hypoxia and fibroblast activation protein (FAP), in gastrointestinal tumors compared with 18F-FDG PET/CT.

Methods

Thirty-two patients with gastrointestinal tumors (21 for initial staging, 11 for restaging) underwent both 68Ga-NI-FAPI and 18F-FDG PET/CT within 1 week. Immunohistochemistry for FAP and hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha (HIF-1α) was performed. Semiquantitative parameters including SUVmax, TBR, MTV, and total lesion FAP expression/glycolysis (TLF/TLG) were compared. Correlations between SUVmax and primary tumor depth, the short diameter of involved lymph nodes, and liver metastases were analyzed.

Results

Immunohistochemistry confirmed FAP expression on cancer-associated fibroblasts and HIF-1α in tumor cytoplasm. 68Ga-NI-FAPI upgraded initial staging in 2 patients (9.52%). Among recurrent patients, its true positive rate was 100% versus 70% for 18F-FDG. 68Ga-NI-FAPI PET/CT demonstrated higher SUVmax and TBR in primary tumors (14.06±6.26 vs. 10.04±6.53, P=0.005; 12.30±6.80 vs. 6.52±4.38, P<0.001), particularly in signet-ring cell carcinoma (SRCC). It detected more metastases than 18F-FDG (306 vs. 263, P=0.003), with higher SUVmax and TBR in involved lymph nodes, liver metastases, peritoneal metastases, and other distant metastases (all P<0.05). SUVmax of 68Ga-NI-FAPI positively correlated with primary tumor depth (r=0.528, P=0.003), the short diameter of involved lymph nodes (r=0.304, P=0.032), and liver metastases (r=0.349, P=0.040).

Conclusion

68Ga-NI-FAPI exhibits superior diagnostic performance in gastrointestinal tumors compared with 18F-FDG, particularly in staging, SRCC evaluation, and metastasis detection. The positive correlation between tumor size and uptake supports its potential for patient selection in ligand-directed radionuclide therapy, establishing it as an effective theranostic agent for gastrointestinal tumors.

papers.title: Perioperative Camrelizumab Plus Chemotherapy in Locally Advanced Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
papers.abstract:
Importance

Despite multimodal treatment, recurrence remains common in patients with resectable locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). Whether perioperative chemoimmunotherapy improves long-term outcomes remains uncertain.

Objective

To estimate the effect of perioperative camrelizumab plus chemotherapy on event-free survival (EFS) compared with standard surgery-based treatment in patients with resectable locally advanced HNSCC.

Design, setting, and participants

The CAMORAL trial was a multicenter, phase 2 randomized clinical trial conducted at 4 academic hospitals in China between October 2020 and March 2024, with data cutoff on April 11, 2025. Patients aged 18 to 75 years with untreated, resectable stage III to IVB HNSCC were assigned to neoadjuvant-adjuvant treatment or control. Analyses used the intention-to-treat population. Data were analyzed from May 2025 to February 2026.

Interventions

Patients were randomized (1:1) to receive two 21-day cycles of neoadjuvant camrelizumab, 200 mg, plus albumin-bound paclitaxel and carboplatin followed by surgery, risk-adapted adjuvant therapy, and maintenance camrelizumab for up to 15 cycles; or upfront surgery followed by standard risk-adapted adjuvant therapy.

Main outcomes and measures

The primary end point was 2-year EFS. Secondary end points included major pathological response (MPR), pathological complete response (pCR), overall survival, 2-year distant metastasis-free survival, 2-year locoregional recurrence-free survival, and safety.

Results

Of 125 included patients, 99 (79.2%) were male, and the mean (SD) age was 56.3 (11.7) years. A total of 63 patients were assigned to the neoadjuvant-adjuvant group and 62 to the control group; the median (IQR) follow-up was 24.6 (16.8-36.5) months. A total of 103 (82.4%) had oral cavity primary tumors. Among 125 patients, the 2-year EFS rate was 77.8% (95% CI, 63.6-87.0) in the neoadjuvant-adjuvant group compared with 46.1% (95% CI, 31.3-59.6) in the control group (hazard ratio, 0.34; 95% CI, 0.17-0.68; P = .001). MPR and pCR were 47.6% (95% CI, 34.9-60.6) and 25.4% (95% CI, 15.3-37.9), respectively, in the neoadjuvant-adjuvant group, with no MPR or pCR events in the control group. The 2-year overall survival rates were 92.0% and 69.1%, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.25; 95% CI, 0.10-0.64); the hazard ratio of 2-year distant metastasis-free survival was 0.15 (95% CI, 0.03-0.68). Grade 3 or higher treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 50 of 63 patients (79.4%) in the neoadjuvant-adjuvant group and 35 of 62 patients (56.5%) in the control group; 1 fatal treatment-emergent adverse event occurred in the control group.

Conclusions and relevance

In this phase 2 randomized clinical trial, perioperative camrelizumab plus chemotherapy significantly improved EFS with manageable toxic effects, supporting evaluation of intensified perioperative immune priming in resectable HNSCC.

Trial registration

ChiCTR.org.cn Identifier: ChiCTR2000037980.

papers.title: Lymphopenia and Circulating Biomarker Dynamics Associated with Clinical Outcome and Toxicity in Pazopanib-Treated Radioiodine-Refractory Thyroid Cancer: Exploratory Analyses from the Pazothyr Trial.
papers.abstract:
Background

Pazopanib showed clinical activity in progressive radioiodine-refractory differentiated thyroid carcinoma (RAIR-DTC), although its use is limited by substantial toxicity not reduced by intermittent treatment. We aimed to identify biomarkers associated with outcome and treatment-related toxicity in these patients.

Methods

This study reported exploratory results related to the Pazothyr trial (NCT01813136) investigating pazopanib efficacy in RAIR-DTC patients. We evaluated lymphopenia and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) from the Pazothyr clinical database (n = 168). Dedicated informed consent for additional plasma and tumor sample collection allowed quantification of plasma angiogenic factors and cytokines at baseline and after one month of pazopanib (n = 111). Immune markers (CD8, FOXP3, CD163, and PDL1) analyzed by immunohistochemistry in archived primary tumors from patients (n = 68) with response or stable disease after 6 months of pazopanib were scored semiquantitatively. Associations with response, progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and substantial treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were evaluated. Given the exploratory nature of this study, no adjustment for multiple comparisons was performed.

Results

At baseline, moderate and severe lymphopenia were associated with shorter PFS, unlike high NLR. Elevated Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor A (VEGF-A), Interleukin 6 (IL-6), and CXCL8 correlated with poorer PFS. High VEGF-A, hepatocyte growth factor (HGF), IL-6, CXCL8, and CXCL9 were associated with shorter OS. X Early changes in placental growth factor (PlGF), HGF, interleukin 12 subunit p40, and CXCL10 were associated with substantial TRAEs. Multivariable analyses identified baseline severe lymphopenia (hazard ratio [HR] = 2.39 [confidence interval or CI 1.27-4.48], p = 0.007) and high CXCL8 (HR = 2.01 [CI 1.26-3.21], p = 0.004) as independent factors associated with progression. High baseline NLR (HR = 2.26 [CI 1.21-4.22], p = 0.01), HGF (HR = 2.37 [CI 1.33-4.20], p = 0.003), and CXCL8 (HR = 2.20 [CI 1.25-3.87], p = 0.006) were similarly associated with death. One-month increases in PlGF (odds ratio [OR] = 2.49 [CI 1.13-5.50], p = 0.024) and HGF (OR = 2.91 [CI 1.32-6.43], p = 0.008) were independently associated with substantial TRAEs. In patients with tumor samples, Programmed cell Death-Ligand 1 (PDL1)-immune cell score (ICS) >1% (HR = 2.05 [CI 1.15-3.66], p = 0.015) was also associated with progression.

Conclusions

Baseline lymphopenia and inflammatory plasma biomarkers were associated with clinical outcome, whereas early changes in circulating factors were associated with substantial TRAEs. These exploratory results require prospective validation in RAIR-DTC patients treated with pazopanib or other VEGF receptor-targeting multikinase inhibitors. The relevance of PDL1-ICS expression for anti-PD1/PDL1-based therapies requires dedicated prospective trials.
